full_judgment:
Record indicates that Rule arising out of petition under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure (for short the Code) was made ready for hearing on 1-6-2002.

2. First-opposite party presented a petition before this Court for vacating order of stay and direction dated 26-1-2002 passed by this Court.

3. The petition for stay appeared in list on 9-7-2002 noting date of hearing on 10-7-2002 as a petition in name of Mr Md Serajul Huque, learned Advocate for petitioners and Mr Md Muzibur Rahman, learned Advocate for first opposite party. On 10-7-2002 petition appeared in list in the name of learned Advocate Md Serajul Huque for petitioners and learned Advocate Mr Md Muzibur Rahman for first opposite party.

4. None appeared for petitioners Mr Md Muzibur Rahman, learned Advocate for first Opposite Party had been present to perform hearing of petition.

5. On 10-7-2002 this Court recorded order that petition be kept with record to be considered at time of hearing of Civil Revision Petition and since Revision Petition was ready for hearing it was posted for hearing on 17-7-2002 and Revision Petition was to appear in the list on 17-7-2002 with names of both sides at top subject to part heard, if any.

6. Today (17-7-2002) this matter appeared in list for hearing as item No. 5 in name of Mr Md Serajul Huque, learned Advocate for petitioners and Mr Md Muzibur Rahman, learned Advocate for first opposite party. Neither Mr Md Serajul Huque, learned Advocate nor any other appeared in Court to support and press Civil Revision petition. Mr Md Muzibur Rahman, learned Advocate, is present to contest Civil Revision Petition and submitted Affidavit-in-opposition controverting material allegations contained in Civil Revision Petition.

<u>7. The matter is taken up for hearing. In Revision Petition under section 115 of the Code, power to be exercised by this Court is supervisory which may be, also, exercised suo mote. This Court is clothed with supplementary power of superintendence and control over judgment, order and action of courts subordinate to this Court. In exercise of this power this Court is not obliged to hear parties in disposing of Civil Revision Petition and a judgment can be pronounced in absence of parties when they have opportunity to appear but fail to appear. For this view taken by me I am fortified with a decision of Appellate Division in Safaruddin and others vs Fazlul Huq and others 49 DLR (AD) 151. In this Revision Petition though none appears in support of Revision Petition in exercise of supervisory power under section 115 of the Code I propose to dispose of the same on merit.</u>

8. The only point that survives for determination in this Civil Revision Petition is whether order under challenge in Revision Petition allowing a petition of defendant-first-opposite party dispensing with service of notices upon Defendants Fourth-Fortieth Opposite Parties warrants any interference by this Court in exercise of it discretionary Civil Revisional Jurisdiction as envisaged under section 115 of the Code and, also, in safe dispensation of justice.

9. A resume of facts essential and requisite to dispose of the point posed is succinctly stated hereunder.

10. Petitioners as plaintiffs instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 8 of 2000 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Amtali, Barguna for a decree of partition with respect to property described in schedule to plaint. First opposite party was Thirty Three Defendant and Fourth-Fortieth Opposite Parties were First-Thirty Two and Thirty Four-Thirty Nine Defendants. Suit was decreed ex parte on 20-11-2001.

11. First opposite party who was Thirty Three Defendant in suit sought setting aside the decree passed ex parte on presentation of a petition under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code. The said petition has been numbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 41 of 2001. In Miscellaneous Case plaintiffs-petitioners were First-Third Opposite Parties and other defendants of suit were Fourth-Fortieth Opposite Parties. First opposite party on 28- 11-2001 laid two petitions; one for dispensation with service of notices upon Fourth-Fortieth-Defendants-Opposite Parties and another for staying the operation of decree recorded in Title Suit No. 8 of 2002.

12. Learned. Assistant Judge by order dated 28-11-2001 under challenge in Revision Petition dispensed with service of notices upon the aforesaid Opposite Parties and, also, stayed operation of impugned ex park decree.

13. Feeling aggrieved, plaintiffs as petitioners approached this Court in this Revision Petition.

14. For purpose of determining the point posed and, also, resolution of legal controversy, it will be profitable to notice rules 13 and 14 of Order IX of the Code.

15. Rule 13 enshrines that in any case in which a decree is passed ex parte against a defendant, he may apply to the Court by which the decree was passed for an order to set it aside and if he satisfies the Court that the summons was not duly served, or that he was prevented by any sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for hearing, the Court shall make an order setting aside the decree as against him.

16. Rule 14 postulates that no decree shall be set aside on any such application as aforesaid unless notice thereof has been served on the opposite party.

17. Notice and opposite party contained in rule 14 may carefully be examined.

<u>18. Rule 13 authorises a defendant to apply to court for setting aside a decree which was awarded in favour of plaintiff or group of plaintiffs who is or are Decree-Holders and Decree if stands set aside that shall be set aside in respect of Decree-Holder plaintiff or group of plaintiffs and not in respect of defendants against whom Decree has been recorded and words "opposite party" shall, thus, mean Decree-Holder. or Decree Holders in whose favour decree was passed. Notice as contemplated under rule 14 is required to be served only upon those opposite party or parties who figured as plaintiff or plaintiffs who had been graced with a decree. This view of mine is fortified with an authority in Sushil Kumar Chowdhury and others vs Annada Prasanna Lahiri and others, AIR 1927 Calcutta 692=31 CWN 906 wherein Division Bench of Calcutta High Court considered the words "opposite party" occurring in rule 14 .and held that the words "opposite party" would mean the plaintiffs who obtained an ex parte decree against defendant.</u>

<u>19. Plaintiffs-decree-holders were only the opposite parties upon whom notices are required to be served and other defendants-opposite parties who were not plaintiffs-decree-holders and not beneficiaries of Decree are not required to be served with notices.</u>

<u>20. In the exercise of discretionary Revisional Jurisdiction under section 115 of the Code this Court shall interfere with any order, Judgment, decision or action of Courts subordinate to it only when it can be demonstratively shown that those suffer from error of law resulting in an error in the decision and by that error a failure of justice has been occasioned. Error of decision of subordinate Court does not by itself justify interference in revision and along with that it is to be manifested that by error a failure of justice has been rendered.</u>

<u>Decision rendered and conclusion reached by learned Assistant Judge, Amtali, Barguna in dispensing with service of notices upon defendants-opposite parties do neither appear to have suffered from any illegality, legal infirmity and error of law nor any failure of justice seem to have been occasioned.</u>

21. Moreover, discretion exercised by learned Assistant Judge in recording the decision under challenge in Revision Petition transpires to have been exercised properly, judiciously and said discretion cannot be characterized to have been exercised arbitrarily and capriciously. Desecration exercised by learned Judge is methodized by analogy and informed by tradition. It is, always, to be remembered that exercise of discretion calculated to advance substantial justice, though not strictly regular and, also, not in accordance with procedure, may not be interfered with in Revision. Procedural law is always subservient to substantial justice and ends of law is nothing but justice. Technicality and procedural hurdles, if any, must bend to substantial justice for which the Court alone exists.

22. No illegality and no error of law had been committed and no failure of justice has been occasioned by the order under challenge in Revision Petition. No interference is, therefore, called for.

23. This Rule arising out of Civil Revision Petition under section 115 of the Code is devoid of any substance and same stands discharged. Order dated 28-11-2001 recorded by learned Assistant Judge, Amtali, Barguna in Miscellaneous Case No. 41 of 2001 springing out of Title Suit No. 8 of 2000 stands good and maintained.

24. Order dated 26-1-2002 staying operation of impugned order dated 28-11-20.01 so far it related to dispensation of service of notice upon Opposite Party Nos. 4-40 stands vacated and direction passed upon Opposite Party No. 1 to put in requisites for service of notices upon Opposite Party Nos. 4-40 and direction recorded upon learned Assistant Judge to issue notice upon Opposite Party Nos. 4-40, also, stand vacated.

25. Miscellaneous Case No. 41 of 2001 laid under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure shall proceed in accordance with law.

No costs.

End.

full_judgment:
Md Nuruzzaman J : On an application under section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure leave was granted consider whether the order under challenge suffers from an error of law resulting in an erroneous decision occasioning failure of justice. Decide the leave granting order the instant Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order complained of in the petition moved in Court today should not be set-aside.

2. The facts necessary, for disposal of the instant Rule, in short, are that the opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 55 of 2013 in the Court of learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Barguna praying for partition of the property schedule of the plaint. The learned Joint District Judge by his judgment and decree dated 13-10-2014 decreed the suit ex-parte. The decree-holder by dint of judgment and decree dated 13-10-2014 filed the Execution Case No. 2 of 2015 in the Court of learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Barguna. In the mean time the instant decree-holder Advocate commissioner was appointed who submitted the report for consideration at the time of preparation of the final decree. Thereafter, the Execution Case was fixed for served the notice the delivery writ of possession upon the petitioner on 6-4-2017.

3. The petitioner judgment-debtor knowing about the judgment and decree against her from one Md Yousuf Ali filed Miscellaneous Case being No.5 of 2016 under Order IX, rule 13 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure hereinafter to be referred as the Code, on 3-4-2016 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Barguna which was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 5 of 2016. The plaintiff-opposite party No.1 has filed the written objection in the Miscellaneous Case.

4. The present petitioner during pendency of the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case filed an application for staying the operation of Title Execution Case No. 2 of 2015 alleging, that no notice was served upon the petitioner. She further alleged that the plaintiff allegedly served a notice at the village house of the husband of the petitioner by fraud practice in fact petitioner and her husband used to live in the Town at DKP Road, Pourashava area, Barguna long before filing of the suit. Therefore, in the facts and circumstances she prayed for staying the operation of the execution case for ends of justice until disposal of the instant Miscellaneous Case.

5. The learned Joint District Judge by his judgment and order dated 22-6-2016 rejected the application of the petitioner for staying the operation of Execution Case No. 2 of 2015. 6. The petitioner being aggrieved by the order dated 22-6-2016 preferred a Civil Revision in the Court of learned District Judge, Barguna being the Civil Revision No. 28 of 2016. The learned Joint District Judge upon hearing both the sides by his judgment and order dated 14-6-2017 rejected the Civil Revision and thereby affirmed the judgment and order dated 22-6-2016 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 5 of 2016.

7. The petitioner being unsuccessfully preferred the instant revisional application under sub-rule 4 of section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure wherein at the time of granting the leave a Division Bench of this Court formulated leave grant order which runs as follows:

"Leave is granted to consider whether the order under challenged suffers from an error of law resulting in an erroneous decisions occasioning failure of justice."

8. Mrs Nahid Yesmin With Mr lqbal Hasan, the learned Advocates appearing for the petitioner has submitted that the learned District Judge has committed a serious error of an important question of law resulting in erroneous decision occasioning failure of justice in affirming the order passed by the Executing Court rejecting an application for stay the operation of the proceedings in the decree Execution Case No. 2 of 2015 arising out of ex-parte judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 55 of 2013 without considering that no notice was served upon the petitioner in the suit as well as execution proceeding and, as such, the impugned order is liable to be set-aside.

9. She has further pointed that learned District Judge has taken erroneous decision without considering that admittedly the petitioner has used to live at DKP Road, Barguna Pourashava, Barguna with her husband and notice of the Title Suit No. 55 of 2013 allegedly served upon the village house of husband of the petitioner who never lived thereon and thereafter, in Title Execution Case No. 2 of 2015 notice of writ of delivery of possession allegedly served upon the petitioner DKP Road, Barguna Pourashava, Barguna from which it is clearly shows that the plaintiff has the malafide intention and in connivance of the others obtained the ex-parte judgment and decree and thereafter they have created the address of the petitioner to proceed with the execution case.

10. She has further added that it is not the case against the husband that he has contested in the suit and the wife does not appear in the suit and now the wife has taken the plea that notice was not served upon her rather, it is the case that no notice was served upon the defendants No. 1-2 because they since long before have been residing in the Barguna Pourashava and notice has been allegedly served in the address of the village home of the defendants.

11. She has further pointed that both the Courts below has taken the erroneous view that if the Court execute the decree and dispossessed the defendants from the suit property they will not suffer in any injury and loss rather, opined that if the petitioner succeed in the Miscellaneous Case in that case the petitioner can recorded the possession of the suit property under section 144 of the Code. However, both the Courts below have forgotten if the pending Miscellaneous Case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code the ex-parte judgment and decree executed the Miscellaneous Case itself would be infructuous. Therefore, both the Courts below committed serious error of law hence, she prayed for make the Rule absolute setting aside the judgment and order of both the Courts below.

12. Opposite party No. 1 contested the suit by filing counter affidavit annexing the order sheet of the Miscellaneous Case No. 5 of 2016.

13. Mr Tareq very candidly submitted that both the Courts below in the judgment has given the cogent reasonings for rejecting the application for stay the operation of the execution case and, as such, the Court below committed no error of law.

14. He has further argued that the petitioner knowing fully well that her husband has received the notice on her behalf now she has come to the Court only to take and frustrate the judgment and decree dated 13-10-2014 which is awaiting to attitude the land and writ of possession has already been issued by the Court after submission of the Advocate Commissioner report.

15. He at the same breath added if the stay of the operation of the Execution Case being case No. 2 of 2015 is granted the opposite party No. 1 would be suffered irreparable loss and injury and he would be deprived of from getting the fruits of the decree which cannot be, rather, according to the opinion of both the Courts below if the petitioner succeed in the Miscellaneous Case she would have take the legal consequence as opined by the both the Courts below so, there is no necessity to interference by this Court in the impugned judgment and order.

16. Mr Tareq very strenuously argued that the notice was served under Rule 20 of Order V of the Code upon the husband of the petitioner which would be determined at the trial of the Miscellaneous Case so, this Court cannot interfere or opined in respect of the service of the notice.

17. We have gone through the order dated 22-6-2016 passed by the learned Joint. District Judge, 1st Court, Barguna in Miscellaneous Case No. 5 of 2016 and judgment and order passed by the learned District Judge in Civil Revision No. 28 of 2016.

18. We have anxiously considered the submissions advanced by the learned Advocate of the respective parties. According to the leave granting order the question before this Court is whether in rejecting the application for stay of the operation of the execution case the Courts below committed an error of law resulting in an erroneous decisions occasioning failure of justice.

19. On perusal of the ex-parte judgment and decree dated 13-10-2014 it appears that the plaintiff Mrs Sabina Sultana was examined as PW No. 1 and some documents have been marked as exhibits 1, 2 and 3. Thereafter, the learned Judge allowed the suit ex-parte. However, on perusal of the judgment and order it is not revealed that during the pendency of the suit the husband of the petitioner was appeared and contested in the suit. So the ground set-forth in the revisional application regarding the service of the notice though under challenged in the Miscellaneous Case filed under Order IX, rule 13 does not come within the purview of the Rule 20 of Order V as argued by the learned Advocate for the opposite parties. Rather, we are of the opinion that both the Courts below opined that if the stay of the operation of the execution case is granted the ex-parte decree obtained by the plaintiff would be frustrated. Therefore, the plaintiff opposite party would be suffered irreparable loss. However, the Courts below before taking the view in favour of plaintiff opposite party they never opined that if ex-parte decree is executed and the execution case is ended with the full satisfaction of the Court the Miscellaneous Case filed under Rule 13 of Order IX of the Code would be frustrated before disposal of the application for stay of the Execution Case for which the multiplicity of the case would be arisen between the parties.

<u>20. We are, therefore, of the considered view that the case of both the sides must be considered in juxta equilibration of the yardstick of justice although we find that the orders passed by the joint District Judge, Barguna and the learned District Judge as revisional Court never discussed any point in respect of the facts of the Miscellaneous Case rather, from their opinion it appears to us that they have taken the view that the ex-parte decree must be executed and the petitioner if succeed in the Miscellaneous Case in that case the petitioner would have a chance to recover the possession of the suit property under section 144 of the Code which adversely gone against the substantive justice. When both the parties under litigation to set-aside the ex-parte judgment and decree the executing Court must born in mind that if the petitioner has not given a chance to prove her allegation of fraud against the plaintiff in obtaining the ex-parte judgment and decree what would be consequence if after conclusion of the trial of Miscellaneous Case the petitioner is able to prove her allegation of fraud and why she would have to face another proceeding as opined by them.</u>

<u>21. Since, the Miscellaneous Case is pending we restrained our self to discuss the merit of the case of the either side but it is very pertinent to mention here that the view taken in disposing the application for stay both the Courts have otherwise decided the consequence of the Miscellaneous Case which is not only a serious error of law rather, outright violation of the settle maxim of law which has been practising in the judicial arena and unhesitatingly violation of the provision of law as enacted in Rule 13 of Order IX of the Code. The Court below if form such an opinion in pending case then mere disposal of ex parte will prevail instead of just and fair justice which will surely not serve the best justice rather, call for more and more litigation.</u>

22. We are, therefore, of the view that it is a fit case to interfere in the impugned judgment and order by this Court otherwise the process of the Court would mot only be frustrated but litigants will suffer unending and fruitless litigation after filing the execution case by dint of ex-parte judgment and decree.

23. Therefore we find that the submissions advanced by the learned Advocate for the petitioner bears merit.

24. Therefore, we find substance in the leave granting order as well as in the instant Rule.

25. Thus, the Rule having merit, it succeeds.

26. In the result, the Rule is made absolute.

27. The judgment and order dated 22-6-2016 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 5 of 2016 by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, and judgment and order dated 14-6-2017 passed by the learned District Judge, Barguna in Civil Revision No. 28 of 2016 is hereby set-aside.

28. The application for stay of the-Execution Case No. 2 of 2015 is allowed.

29. The further proceedings and stay the operation of the Execution Case is hereby stayed till disposal of the Miscellaneous Case No. 5 of 2016.

30. However, the Executing Court is directed to dispose of the Miscellaneous Case No. 5 of 2016 expeditiously within 6 (six) months from the date of receipt of the judgment positively.

The office is directed to communicate the judgment and order to the Court below at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Soumendra Sarker, J: The Rule issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 05.05.2004 passed by the learned District Judge, Mymensingh in Civil Revision No.18 of 2004 rejecting the said revisional application summarily and refusing to stay all further proceedings of Other Class Execution Case No. 08 of 2002 should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the opposite party as plaintiff instituted the original suit for Specific performance of Contract being Other Class Suit No. 52 of 1993 in the 1st Court of the then Subordinate Judge, Mymensingh contending inter alia that the owner of the suit land, defendant entered into a contract with the plaintiff for selling the suit land at a consideration of Taka 2,60,000/= and on taking Taka 70,000/= as earnest money, the defendant executed a Baynapatra on 23.06.1992 and one year time was fixed for payment of the rest consideration amount. Subsequently, the plaintiff paid Taka 20,000/= on different dates and in this way Taka 90,000/= was paid and Taka 1,70,000/= remained unpaid. Lastly, at the denial of the defendant to execute and register a sub-kabala deed in favour of the plaintiff, the plaintiff instituted the original suit.

3. The contrary case of the defendant in short is such that he did not execute the alleged bainapatra dated 23.06.1992 for selling the suit land and only in need of some money on taking a sum of Taka 90,000/= from the plaintiff, he mortgaged the suit property, but the plaintiff subsequently out of ill motive without taking the mortgaged amount instituted the original suit after creating a false bainapatra, for Specific Performance of Contract.

4. The Original Other Class Suit No. 52 of 1993 for want of defendant's hazira was decreed ex parte on 15.08.1995. Subsequently, the defendant knowing about the ex parte decree filed a Miscellaneous Case being No. 97 of 1995 for setting aside the same. The said Miscellaneous Case was dismissed on 12.05.1998. Thereafter, the plaintiff instituted the Other Class Execution Case No. 08 of 2002 on 30.11.2002. During pendency of that execution case the Defendant-Judgment-debtor filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 20.01.2004 for setting aside the execution case on the ground of limitation. The learned Executing Court while rejected that application on 06.04.2004, the Defendant-Judgment debtor being aggrieved filed a Civil Revision being No. 18 of 2004 before the learned District judge, Mymensingh and the learned District Judge by the impugned order dated 05.05.2004 summarily rejected the revisional application.

5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order of the 1st Court of revision, the Defendant-Judgment debtor-Petitioner has preferred 2nd revision with leave of this Court and obtained the Rule with an interim order of stay.

6. During hearing of this Rule Mr. Probir Neogi, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioners i.e. the legal heirs of the original Defendant-Judgment debtor, while Mr. Khandaker Aminul Haque, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the Plaintiff-Decree holder-Opposite party.

7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned 1st Court of revision as well as the executing Court during passing its judgment and orders committed illegality and irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned District Judge, Mymensing misdirected himself in grasping the factual aspect of the case, as well as erred in law in deciding the fate of the revisional application. The learned Counsel in his submission argued that on the ground of law point, which is based on the period of limitation for filing of the execution case, the application for setting aside the execution proceedings was filed by the Judgment debtor-Petitioner, but neither the executing court nor the 1st court of revision has been able to appreciate the proposition of law as provided in Article 182 of the Limitation Act. The learned Advocate submits that the decree was passed on 15.08.1995 but the execution case was filed on 30.11.2002, which is apparently time barred as it was filed seven years, three months, fifteen days after the decree. The learned Advocate also submits that under Article 182 of the Limitation Act, 1908 the period of limitation is only 03 (three) years and within this period the execution case shall have to be filed, but apparently the execution case was not filed within that period. The learned Counsel referring a decision of our Apex Court reported in 05 BLC (AD) 07 submits that the Decree holder-Opposite party fraudulently obtained the kabala deed registered through court in the above mentioned execution case, but in fact; the execution of the decree was no longer alive when it was enforced by the alleged execution and registration of the kabala deed through court. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the kabala deed which was obtained through a void execution proceedings is a nullity in the eye of law.

8. As against the aforesaid submission of the learned Counsel for the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party opposing the Rule submits that the Execution Case being No. 08 of 2002 while was proceeding, there was no order of stay from any higher court and there was no legal embargo in the proceedings of the execution case and accordingly the executing court exhausted all the process of execution and the decree was executed properly by registration of the sub-kabala deed through court in favour of the Defendant-Opposite party. After filing a counter-affidavit, the learned Advocate for the Plaintiff-Opposite party argued that the Other Class Suit No. 52 of 1993 was decreed ex parte on 15.08.1995. Thereafter, the Plaintiff-Decree holder filed Other Class Execution Case No. 08 of 2002. The learned Joint District Judge executed the kabala deed in favour of the Decree holder in pursuance of the order dated 09.07.2009 and accordingly passed necessary order for registration of the said deed. Thereafter on 27.06.2013 the kabala deed being No. 6891 was registered on 02.07.2013 vide Annexure-‘1’. The learned Advocate further submits that the kabala deed was duly executed and registered through court and the entire process of the execution case was lawful and handing over the suit land to the Decree holder was held at the time of execution of the ‘bainapatro’ and thereby the entire process of the execution case has been finalized and confirmed. The learned Advocate lastly submits that, at this stage there is nothing to interfere with the execution proceedings since the cause of action of this civil revision has been ceased by disposal of the execution case.

9. In order to appreciate the submission advanced from the side of the learned Counsels for the parties, having gone through the connected papers including the ex parte decree passed by the learned trial court dated 15.08.1995 in Other Class Suit No. 52 of 1993, the application of the Plaintiff-Decree holder dated 10.11.2003 (Annexure-‘D’) for starting the Decree Execution Case, the application filed by the Judgment debtor under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure dated 20.01.2004 for rejection of the Decree Execution Case No. 08 of 2002 (Annexure-‘E’), the order of the executing court dated 22.02.2004 (Annexure-‘F’), the order dated 06.04.2004 of the same court in Execution Case No. 08 of 2002 [Annexure-F (1)], the order of the learned Joint District Judge, of the same proceedings dated 25.04.2004 (Annexure-‘G’), the order dated 11.05.2004 of the executing court (Annexure-‘H’) and the impugned order of the court of revision dated 05.05.2004, it transpires that the original suit for Specific Performance of Contract being No. 52 of 1993 was decreed on 15.08.1995. After that decree, the Defendant-Judgment debtor-Petitioner filed an application for setting aside that ex parte decree under Order IX rule 13 along with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure being Miscellaneous Case No. 97 of 1995. The learned trial court by its judgment and order dated 12.05.1998 disallowed the aforesaid miscellaneous case vide Annexure-‘C’. Thereafter, the Decree holder-Opposite party to this civil revision filed an application for starting the Execution Case on 10.11.2003 vide Annexure-‘D’. It also transpires from the connected papers that the Judgment debtor-Petitioner against the decree execution case stating that the case is time barred filed an application before the executing court on 20.01.2004 to reject the execution proceeding. Subsequently, the learned executing court after different dates on 06.04.2004 rejected that application of the Judgment debtor holding the view that the execution case is not barred by limitation. The Judgment debtor thereafter preferred the 1st Civil Revision being No. 18 of 2004 and filed an application on 25.04.2004 before the executing court supported by an information slip from the court of the learned District Judge, Mymensingh praying for an order of stay of the execution proceedings. The learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh without disposal of the said application fixed a date on 11.05.2004 for hearing on that application and deficit stamp papers from the side of the Decree holder. I also find that on the date Fixed i.e. on 11.05.2004 the learned executing court fixed another date on 30.05.2004 for deficit stamp papers for the kabala deed and in the meanwhile the court obtained the order of rejection of the Civil Revision No. 18 of 2004 of the learned District Judge, Mymensingh.

<u>10. On meticulous consideration of the papers in connection of the factual aspects of the case, it is evident from the face of the papers that the learned 1st court of revision while passing the impugned order dated 05.05.2004, the execution proceeding was continuing and a date was fixed ahead for depositing the deficit stamp papers. Furthermore, it is noticed that the learned District Judge, Mymensing without going into the legal aspect of the revisional application filed before him in a slipshod manner, by passing the mandatory provision of law as incorporated in Article 182 of the limitation Act, 1908 passed the impugned order dated 05.05.2004 in hasty way, which is imprudent in nature. Obviously, the learned 1st court of revision failed to apply his judicial mind during passing the impugned judgment and order and as such the order itself is not in accordance with law. I also find from the relevant laws that in a execution case for the execution of a decree, the Decree holder has no other alternative but to file the execution case within 03 (three) years from the date of decree.</u>

<u>11. It is well settled that in the limitation Act, 1908 Article 182 requires a 1st  application for execution of decree to be made within 03 (three) years of the decree, and the each successive application is to be made within 03 (three) years of the final order. Hence, an application for execution has to satisfy firstly, Article 182 of the Limitation Act, 1908 being the earliest period prescribed and secondly, Section 48 of the Code of Civil Procedure which prescribes the maximum period of limitation. In this context, it is apparent to note that if the execution petition is hit by any of the two provisions, it is to fail. [Ref. 36 DLR (AD) 5; BCR 1983 (AD) 418; 48 DLR (AD) 141; 53 DLR 78]</u>

12. Having regard to the decisions referred to from the sides of the respective parties in this instant Civil Rule, I am constrained to hold such a view that our Apex Court's decision is very much clear with regard to filing of the execution proceeding and the period of limitation as prescribed in Article 182 of the Limitation Act (IX of 1908) is 03 (three) years and within this period the Decree holder shall have to file an application for execution of the decree and the court is empowered to proceed with the execution proceedings in that case only. But in the instant case as I have come across from the relevant papers that the executing court was not lawful in the proceedings of the Execution Case No. 08 of 2002, inasmuch as; the said execution case was time barred. Therefore, the subsequent acts of the executing court are not valid in the eye of law. It is crystal clear that the executing court proceeded with the execution proceedings without jurisdiction and as such the sub-kabala deed which was registered through court by the said execution proceeding is void ab initio, which need not be avoided. The kabala deed which was obtained through court by the aforesaid illegal proceedings was obtained fraudently and as such it is a nullity.

13. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and order dated 05.05.2004 passed by the learned District Judge, Mymensingh in Civil Revision No.18 of 2004 rejecting the said revisional application summarily and refusing to stay all further proceedings of Other Class Execution Case No. 08 of 2002 is hereby set aside.

14. The order of stay granted earlier by this court at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated.

15. Communicate the judgment and order at once.

End.

full_judgment:
This Rule has been issued calling upon the Opposite Parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 27-3-2012, passed by the learned District Judge, Khagrachari Hill District, in Civil Appeal No.8 of 2009, dismissing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and order dated 4-2-2009, passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Khagrachari Hill District, in Civil Suit No.67 of 2006, should not be set-aside and/or pass such other order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts, relevant for disposal of the Rule, in brief, are that one Farid Ahmed Bhuiyan, as plaintiffs, filed the Civil Suit No.67 of 2006 in the court of Joint District Judge, Khagrachari Hill District against Amir Hossain and others, being the defendants, under sections 8/9 of the Specific Relief Act.

3. The defendants have contested in the suit by filing written statements denying the material averments made in the plaint.

4. The Trial Court, by its judgment and order dated 4-2-2009, has dismissed the suit mainly for the reasons that, the defendants are occupying the suit property for more than 12 years and they were possessing the suit property by way of adverse possession.

5. Against the said judgment and order of the Trial Court, the present petitioner, preferred Civil Appeal No.8 of 2009 (as appellant) before the District Judge, Khagrachari Hill District, who being the Appellate Court, has passed the impugned judgment and order dismissing the appeal by affirming the judgment and order of the trial court, vide judgment and order dated 27-3-2012.

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order of the Appellate Court, the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner has filed this application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule.

7. Mr Md Abdur Rouf, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner having drawn my attention to the lower court's record, first of all submits that, by an order No. 9 dated 19-11-2008 of the trial court, it had fixed for hearing of a temporary injunction petition, but there was no such petition for temporary injunction. However, he proceeds on the court then fixed 13-1-2009 for hearing of temporary injunction. He also submits that, on that date, the trial court records to have heard the matter and fixed for delivery of the judgment on 21-1-2009. But, on 21-1-2009 the trial court noted that it was busy in other government works, as it appears from the order sheet and then, the matter has been fixed on 29-1-2009 for pronouncing judgment and then again deferred to 4-2-2009. He then submits that, ultimately, on 4-2-2009, the trial court has pronounced the judgment without taking any evidence, oral or documentary, and without hearing any submission on merit and, as such, the trial court had violated the procedural law in pronouncing the judgment and decree and the said judgment and decree was not based on any evidence, whatsoever. Therefore, the learned Advocate continues that, the appellate court, without paying any heed to the fact that the suit was fixed on 13-1-2009 for hearing of the temporary injunction and the suit was not at all heard in accordance with law and that no evidence could be placed before the trial court, had dismissed the suit and has mechanically passed the impugned judgment and decree. The learned Advocate further submits that, the appellate court also dittoed the same decision of the trial court and the impugned judgment has occasioned failure of justice and caused serious prejudice to the petitioner. He next submits that, the findings of the trial court as regards the adverse possession are not based on any evidence on record and a trespasser cannot claim any title on the basis of adverse possession. Accordingly, the Rule has merits and the same may be made absolute, he prays.

8. None has appeared on behalf of the opposite parties though the matter has been appearing in the cause list for more than one week, with the names of the learned Advocates of parties.

9. I have heard the learned Advocate of the petitioner, perused the application for revision, lower Court's record as well as the judgment of both the Courts below and other materials in the record.

10. I find that, one Farid Ahmed Bhuiyan, as plaintiff, had filed this suit and the defendants had contested in the suit by filing written statements. I also find that, the trial court by its order No. 9, dated 19-11-2008, had fixed the case for hearing of a temporary injunction petition. It further appears from the trial court's order No. 10, dated 13-1-2009 that, the trial court has recorded to have heard the suit and, therefore, fixed on 21-1-2009 for pronouncing judgment. Then on 21-1-2009 the trial court has recorded that, it was busy in other government works (not judicial works) and had deferred the matter for pronouncing judgment to 29-1-2009 and then again to 4-2-2009, and, ultimately, on 4-2-2009, the trial court had pronounced the judgment without taking any evidence, oral or documentary. As such, the trial court has violated the procedural law in hearing the suit and in pronouncing the judgment and decree and the said judgment and decree was not based on evidence whatsoever.

11. The trial court ought to have given an opportunity, to the parties, to adduce evidence and, as such, the trial court has passed the judgment, without taking any evidence holding that, the defendants were occupying the suit property for more than 12 years and had acquired title by way of adverse possession, although such finding of adverse possession is based on no evidence.

12. I hold that, any trespasser or land grabber, however long the period of possession might be, never acquires, nor can claim any title in any property in the name of or on the excuse of adverse possession. No court, nor any other authority can confer any title, on the excuse of adverse possession, to a trespasser or a land grabber continuing in possession for any period of time, even if that be more than 12 (twelve) years. Court of law should not perpetuate any illegality. In order to succeed on the basis of adverse possession, the occupant must prove some legal basis, however weak or at least a bonafide claim or an equitable right to show his peaceful entry into and continuation in the possession, with express or implied consent and knowledge of the rival claimant. If the fact of illegal possession has been kept suppressed by resorting to any fraud, forgery, illegal threat or force, then such possession, however long it might be, shall be of no use. On the contrary, if the rival claimant (or his/her/their predecessor) was a party to or has otherwise acquiesced in giving or surrendering or handing over of or parting with such possession, then the same should confer ( in the possessor) the benefit of adverse possession. Everything will depend on proper evidence and findings.

13. The conduct of the trial judge Mr Md Abdul Hamid, the then Joint District Judge, Khagrachari Hill District, who has passed the judgment and decree, prima-facie shows his serious lack of knowledge and his conduct also raises question about the propriety of his conduct. Similarly, the conduct of Mr Md Amirul Islam, the then District Judge, Khagrachari Hill District, who was judge of the appellate court, is also uncalled for. His judgment was not based on any oral or documentary evidence on record and he has mechanically dismissed the appeal, which is bound to shake public confidence in the administration of justice system, only for such non-judicious conduct of a countable few.

14. It has also to be recorded here that, as per the averments made in the plaint, the trial court ought to have framed issues and ought to have taken evidence and decide as to whether the suit for recovery of possession under section 8/9 of the Specific Relief Act was maintainable or not, without a prayer for declaration of title alongwith consequential relief for recovery of khash possession, on payment of ad-valorem proper court fess.

<u>15. It is hereby decided and directed that, if either of the parties cannot prove their lawful title in the suit property, then the entire property shall go to and be recorded in the name of the Government. in Khash Khatian and the court shall pass a judgment accordingly.</u>

16. The trial court is further directed to consider (as per law) the application, if any, filed by either party to amend their pleadings and also to add the Government, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Khagrachari, as pro-forma defendant, should cause amendment in the cause title of the plaint accordingly and should issue summons upon the Government, before proceeding further.

17. The findings of the trial court and those of the appellate court are hereby set aside, since not based on any evidence.

18. The trial court should comply with the direction of this Court as it is binding upon it, as per Article 109 of the Constitution.

19. In view of the deliberation, recorded above, I find merit in this Rule.

Order

In the result, the Rule is made absolute and the suit is sent back on remand for fresh trial in view of the directions given and the observations made above.

The impugned judgment and order dated 27-3-2012, passed by the learned District Judge, Khagrachari Hill District, in Civil Appeal No.8 of 2009, dismissing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and order dated 4-2-2009, passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Khagrachari Hill District, in Civil Suit No.67 of 2006, are hereby be set-aside. The findings arrived at by them shall stand reversed.

No costs.

Copies of this judgment be sent to the courts concerned alongwith the LCR at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana J: This appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated 10-12-2002 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4745 of 2001 discharging the Rule.

2. The appellants, as plaintiffs, instituted Title Suit No. 85 of 1995 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Naria, Shariatpur against the defendant-respondent Nos. 1 to 13 praying for a declaration that the ex-parte decree dated 25-7-1989 passed in Title Suit No. 41 of 1988 is null and void, fraudulent, collusive, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs' case, in short, is that Mohendra Chandra Karati, Kamini Bewa, Sona Bewa and Sitalazmi Bewa were the owners of 4.11 acres of land of RS Khatian No. 197 of mouja Panchagaon, Police Station-Naria. That Mahendra Chandra Karati-who was the owner in possession of the 8 anas share transferred some land to Tarai Haider and others by a registered kabala dated 6-11-1975; Mahendra Chandra Karati sold out his rest land to Nurjahan Begum by registered saf-kabala dated 19-12-1975 and put her in possession of the said land. That Nurjahan Begum while owning and possessing that land sold out 24 decimals of land to the plaintiff No. 1 and 6 decimals of land to the plaintiff No. 2 by registered saf-kabalas dated 23-4-1983. That Arab Ali Howlader and others while were owners in possession of the land in plot No. 1846 sold out 10 decimals of land by registered kabala dated 26-11-1986 to the predecessor of the plaintiff Nos. 4 to 14. That Elahi Box Mridha-another purchaser of the suit land died leaving behind two daughters, namely Nasima Khatun and Hazera Khatun and wife Shamsun Nahar and the said heirs of Elahi Box Mirdha sold out 32 decimals of land of suit plot No. 1846 to the plaintiff No. 3 by registered kabalas dated 18-4-1987. That proforma-defendant No. 12 Khalil Mridha has been in possession of 10 decimals of land in the suit plot by purchase. The plaintiffs further case was that Dhirendra Chandra Mondal and others, as plaintiffs, instituted Title Suit No. 124 of 1987 in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Naria impleading the plaintiffs and others as defendants, but that suit was ultimately dismissed for default on 7-2-1987. That the plaintiffs while were in peaceful possession of the suit land came to know on 4th Bhadra 1402 BS from one Kadir Box Mirdha that the predecessor of the defendants, namely, Taleb Ali Saiyal obtained an ex-parte decree in respect of the suit land and upon making necessary inquires the plaintiffs learnt that Taleb Ali Saiyal instituted Title Suit No. 41 of 1988 in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Naria, Shariatpur impleading Mahendra Chandra Karati, an Indian citizen and the Deputy Commissioner, Shariatpur as defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and obtained an ex-parte decree on 25-7-1989 falsely showing the service of summons and without impleading the plaintiffs and the defendants of Title Suit No. 124 of 1987. The plaintiffs alleged that they did not know anything about the ex-parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 41 of 1988.

3. The defendant Nos. 1 to 11 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement contending, inter-alia, that Mahendra Chandra Karati being owner in possession of 82 decimals of land of suit plot No. 1846 entered into a contract with the predecessor of the defendants, namely, Taleb Ali to sell the said land to him at a consideration of Taka 1,500 and executed a bainapatra on 21st Jaistha, 1370 BS with the stipulation that Mahendra Chandra Karati would execute and register the kabala deed in favour of Taleb Ali upon. obtaining necessary papers Taleb Ali's and after death his heirs have been in possession of the suit land since then for more than 12 years and thus have acquired valid title therein, but the employee of the Deputy Commissioner threatened them with dispossession and hence they instituted title Suit No. 41 of 1988 for declaration of title and obtained an ex-parte decree from the Court of the Assistant Judge, Naria, Shariatpur. That the plaintiffs have no right, title and possession in the suit land and that the deeds claimed by the plaintiffs are all false and fabricated.

4. The trial court, on consideration of the evidence adduced by both the parties, dismissed the suit of the plaintiff holding that the alleged registered sale deeds of the plaintiffs' alleged vendors dated 6-12-1975 and 19-12-1975-the exhibits-5,6 and 7 were all void documents as those were registered in the Sub-registrar's Office which had no jurisdiction to register those documents and as such the recipients of those documents-the exhibits-5, 6 and 7 did not acquire any title in the suit land and consequently the plaintiffs also could not acquire title in the suit land by a virtue of purchase from the recipients of those kabalas by the subsequent kabalas dated 23-4-1984, 26-11-1986 and 18-4-1987 the exhibits-1, 2, 3 and 4. The trial court further found that the suit land has not been properly described. Against that judgment and decree of the trial court the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No. 28 of 2000 before the learned District Judge, Shariatpur. The said appeal was ultimately heard and disposed of by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Shariatpur. This appellate court below concurred with the findings and decision of the trial court and thus dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial court. The plaintiffs then preferred the above mentioned civil revision and obtained Rule. A Single Bench of the High Court Division, after hearing both the parties, discharged that Rule affirming the concurrent findings and decision of the courts of facts. The High Court Division also, on examination of the evidence on record, found that the suit land is situated within the jurisdiction of Naria Sub-Registry Office, but the plaintiffs vendors' alleged kabalas dated 6-12-1975 and 19-12-1975 were registered in the Sub-Registry Offices of Kartickpur and Jajira and as such all these three kabalas-the exhibits-5, 6 and 7 were void and that by these void kabalas the plaintiffs alleged predecessors-in-interest could not acquire any right, title and interest in the suit land and consequently the plaintiffs also could not acquire any right, title and interest in the suit land by virtue of alleged purchase by the kabalas dated 23-4-1984, 26-11-1986 and 18-4-1987-the exhibits-1, 2, 3 and 4. The High Court Division concurred also with the decision of the courts of facts that since the plaintiff could not acquire any right, title and interest in the suit land they have no locus standi to challenge the decree passed in Title Suit No. 41 of 1988 in respect of the suit land. The High Court Division upheld also the findings and decision of the appellate court below that the plaintiffs could not prove their possession in the suit land and that the defendants had been able to prove their possession in the suit land.

5. Being aggrieved by this judgment and order of the High Court Division the plaintiff-petitioners filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 902 of 2003 before this Division. This Division granted leave to consider the submissions of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-petitioners which has been stated in the leave granting order thus:

"Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioners, firstly contended that having regard to the provisions of sections 6 and 7 of the Registration Act, permitting a Sub-Registrar perform the duties of a Registrar, the Court below including the High Court Division committed an error of law in discarding the registered documents on the mere plea of different Sub-registry registering the documents against the presumption of law that the official acts are duly performed and in such view of the matter, the findings and decisions of the High Court Division cannot be sustained in law. Mr Mohammad Ali next contended that the instant suit being a suit for setting aside ex-parte decree on the ground of fraud and the trial court having clearly found that the suit in which the ex-parte decree was obtained was incompetent, the courts below including the High Court Division erred in law in holding that the present suit was not maintainable at the instance of the plaintiffs."

<u>6. At the time of hearing this appeal Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, the learned Counsel for the plaintiff-appellants has made the same submissions. The learned Counsel did not dispute the fact that the suit land is situated within the jurisdiction of the Sub-Registrar's Office at Naria. The plaintiffs vendors' alleged kabalas dated 6-12-1975 and 19-12-1975 the exhibits-5 to 7 were registered in the Sub-Registry Offices of Kartickpur and Jajira. The learned Counsel did not dispute or challenge the provision of law that if any document is registered by a Sub-Registrar within whose jurisdiction no portion of the property mentioned in the document is situated, that document is void. The learned Counsel has contended that in view of the provision of sections 6, 7 and 30 of the Registration Act the registration of the plaintiffs vendors' kabala deeds in the sub-registry offices of Kartickpur and Jajira cannot be said illegal and as such those deeds cannot be called void. But we fail to understand the above contention of the learned Counsel for the plaintiff-appellants. Section 6 of the Registration Act has provided for appointment of Registrars and Sub-Registrars by the government. Section 7 of this Registration Act has provided that the government shall establish in every district an office of the Registrar and in every sub-district an office or offices of the Sub-Registrar or of Joint Sub-Registrars and has further provided that the government may amalgamate with any office of a Registrar on any office of a Sub-Registrar subordinate to such Registrar, and may authorize any Sub-Registrar whose office has been so amalgamated to exercise and perform, in addition to his own powers and duties, all or any of the powers and duties of the Registrar to whom he is subordinate. Section 30 of the Registration Act has provided that any Registrar may in his discretion receive and register any document which might be registered by any Sub-Registrar subordinate to him. The learned Counsel for the plaintiff-appellants could not bring any material before us to show that at that relevant time offices of the Sub-Registrars of Kartickpur and Jajira were amalgamated with the office of the Registrar and the Sub-Registrars of those sub-registry offices were authorized to exercise and perform all or any powers and duties of the Registrar to whom they were subordinate. In this suit, before the trial court or even before the appellate court below and the High Court Division, no such plea was ever raised that at that relevant time the Sub-Registrars of Kartickpur and Jajira Sub-Registry Offices were authorized by the government to perform the powers and duties of the Registrar. So, in the circumstances this plea of the learned Counsel for the plaintiff-appellants that the plaintiffs vendors kabala deeds-the exhibits-5, 6 and 7 are not void-cannot be accepted at all.</u>

7. Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, the learned Counsel for the plaintiff-appellants has argued also that in this suit the plaintiffs have prayed for setting aside the ex-parte decree on the ground of fraud and that the trial court also has found that the suit in which this impugned ex-parte decree was passed was incompetent. The learned Advocate has contended that in the circumstances the courts below committed wrong in dismissing the suit on the mere finding that the title deed of the plaintiffs' predecessors-in-interest were void. The learned Counsel has contended that since the trial court found the impugned ex-parte decree not legal it should have set aside this decree. But this argument also of the learned Advocate is not acceptable. All the three courts below have concurrently found that the plaintiffs could not acquire any right, title and interest in the suit land and as such they have no locus standi to challenge the impugned ex-parte decree passed in respect of the suit land. We endorse this concurrent finding and decision of the courts below. The plaintiffs having no right, title and interest in the suit land cannot challenge any decree of a court of law passed in respect of the suit land. The plaintiffs have no locus standi to challenge any decree passed in respect of the suit land.

8. So, we find no merit in this appeal.

Hence this appeal be dismissed on contest without any order as to cost.

End.

full_judgment:
On an application under section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 "(the Code)" leave was granted and Rule was issued calling upon the opposite-party No. 1 to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 11-8-2015 passed by the learned District Judge, Rajshahi in Civil Revision No. 75 of 2014 rejecting the revisional application and affirming the judgment and order dated 25-11-2014 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Durgapur, Rajshahi in Miscellaneous Case No. 16 of 2013 allowing the Miscellaneous Case filed by the defendant under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code and thereby restoring the Partition Suit No. 102 of 2007 to its file and number should not be set inside and/or why such other or further order or orders should not be passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. At the same time of leave granting order dated 13-12-2015, the proceedings of Partition Suit No. 102 of 2007 then pending in the Court of Assistant Judge, Durgapur, Rajshahi was stayed for a period of 6 (six) months from date and pending hearing of the Rule the parties were directed to maintain status quo in respect of possession and position of the suit land for a period of 6 (six) months from date. However, the period of stay and the order of direction of maintaining status quo have not been extended further.

3. The case of the petitioner as made out in the revisional application, in short, is that the petitioner as plaintiff filed Partition Suit No. 102 of 2007 on 11-11-2007 contending, inter alia, that the suit land as mentioned in the schedule of the plaint belonged to Fazullah Prang. Said Fazullah Prang died leaving behind a son, the opposite-party No. 1, the plaintiff-petitioner and the predecessor-in-interest of the opposite-parties Nos. 2-8 as his legal heirs. The heirs of Fazullah Prang are possessing the property. The petitioner being the heir got four annas share and while he has been possessing the same some difficulties has arisen between the co-sharers therefore the plaintiff proposed to the other co-sharers for amicable partition but the later refused to make partition on 18-10-2017. Therefore, the petitioner finding no other alternative resorted to file the suit for partition for getting saham separately as his share. It has been stated in the petition that in spite of serving the notices upon the defendants they failed to appear in the Court for contesting the suit. The trial Court decreed the suit ex-parte against the defendants on 19-4-2009. Accordingly, the petitioner got saham in respect of share of the scheduled properties and the trial Court directed to effect partition amicable by metes and bounds within 40 (forty) days from the date of the decree. When the plaintiff did not get the suit properties pursuant to the decree, a survey knowing Advocate Commissioner was appointed for effective partition and accordingly, Advocate Commissioner submit-ted his report and the partition suit was finally decreed on 7-3-2012. The petitioner as decree holder filed Execution Case No. 2 of 2012, whereby he got his saham through Court on 9-7-2013. At that stage, the opposite-party No. 1 Md Ahsan Prang filed Miscellaneous Case No. 16 of 2013 under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex-parte decree and for restoration of the suit with a separate application for condonatoin of delay of 4 years 3 months 13 days under section 5 of the Limitation Act, which was allowed on 25-11-2014 and thereby restored the Partition Suit No. 102 of 2007 to its file and number.

4. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment and order dated 25-11-2014, the petitioner preferred Civil Revision No. 75 of 2014 before the District Judge, Rajshahi who upon hearing the parties rejected the Civil Revision on contest. Being aggrieved the plaintiff as petitioner approached this Court and obtained the leave as stated above.

5. Mr Md Khariul Alam, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner having drawn the attention of this Court to the Rule 19A of Order V of the Code submits that the onus to prove that summons was duly served upon the defendant is on the plaintiff but the plaintiff can discharge his onus of proof showing the report of the process server along with a declaration that the process server served the summons and the onus is to be shifted upon the defendant to prove that the summons were not served in accordance with law.

6. He next submits that since the process server submitted his report to the trial Court along with a declaration in favour of due services of summons, onus shifted to the defendant that summons were not duly served upon him.

7. Mr Md Khairul Alam, learned Advocate seeks to rely on the decision in the case of Md Insan Ali vs Mir Abdus Salam reported in 40 DLR (AD) 193.

8. In contrast to the submissions of the learned Advocate of the petitioner, Mr Shariful Islam, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite-party No. 1 submits that according to the process server report the summons were served upon one Md Moksed Ali, son of the defendant who allegedly received the same on 21-11-2007 in presence of one Md Khorshed Alam and Md Israfil but the petitioner failed to bring the process server or the attesting witnesses to the Court in order to prove that the summons were duly served upon the defendant.

9. The learned Advocate for the opposite-party next submits that both the courts below concurrently found that the summons were not duly served upon the defendants and, as such, this Court sitting on revisional jurisdiction under section 115(4) of the Code should not interfere into the concurrent findings of the courts below.

10. Heard the submissions of the learned Advocates and perused the materials on record including the provisions of law particularly the issue of service of summons.

11. It appears that on 9-7-2013, the petitioner went to get possession of the suit land pursuant to the ex-parte decree and thereafter the defendant-opposite-party got definite information upon collecting an information slip dated 28-7-2013 about the ex-parte decree. The defendant filed Miscellaneous Case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code for setting aside the ex-parte decree and for restoration of the suit to its file and number with a delay of 4 years 3 months and 13 days. The Miscellaneous Case was filed within 30 (thirty) days from the date of knowledge of the ex-parte decree. The defendant-opposite-party examined himself as PW 1 and his son Md Moksed Ali deposed as PW 2, while the plaintiff-petitioner produced and examined 5 (five) witnesses as D.Ws including DW 5 Nayabe Nazir of the Court concerned. The positive findings of the courts below with regard to service of summons of the process server that it was not duly served upon the opposite-party-defendant herein with strict compliance with the provisions of law. It appears that Md Moksed Ali PW 2 of the Miscellaneous Case deposed that he did not receive the summons on behalf of his father on 21-11-2007. In these circumstances, it is to be noted here that service of summons on a male number of the family would not constitute valid service unless the report of the process server contains a statement that there was no likelihood or the defendant who was absent at the time of service being not found at his residence with a reasonable time, the process server's report must set out his action in full that the defendant was not found, without stating what effort was made to find him is not acceptable in law. In the instant case, on a reading of the report of the process server, I do not find that the mode of searching of the defendant was exhausted by the process server at all.

<u>12. The rule 70 of the CRO requires service of summons in presence of two independent local witnesses. From the report of process server, it could not be ascertained that the attesting witnesses who identified the house of the defendant are the persons of the locality since there is no address in his report dated 21-11-2007. With regard to the registered post, it appears that postal receipt shows that on 26-11-2007, the defendant received the summons putting his signature. The learned Judge compared the signature of the defendant with the signature of postal receipt and the signature appearing in the Okalatnama and the deposition sheet of the defendant are not the same. This being the concurrent finding of the courts below, this Court sitting on a revisional jurisdiction under section 115(4) of the Code cannot interfere into such finding of the courts below accept on an error of law of an important question of law resulting in an erroneous decision passed by the courts below. It further appears from the deposition of the petitioner' side that they failed to prove that the summons were duly served upon the defendant. The process server or the attesting witnesses who identified the house of the defendant were not brought into the Court to prove that the service was duly served upon the defendant. On a reading of rule 19A of Order V of the Code, it appears that this rule shows that service return duly submitted is to be accepted as evidence of the facts as to the service of summons but the rule does not give a go by to the mandatory provisions of rule 19 of Order V of the Code.</u>

<u>13. The rule 19 provides for examination of serving officer with an endorsement that the Court shall verify from the deposition of serving officer whether the summons were served or not in a mandatory form. The word shall makes it clear as appearing in rule 19 of Order V that it is mandatory upon the Court to examine the serving officer to ascertain as to whether the summons were duly served, or not. There is no doubt summons may be served upon an adult member of the defendant family under the provisions of rule 15 of Order V of the Code as has been done in the instant case but both the courts below concurrently disbelieved that the summons was duly served upon the defendant. In case of allegation of non-service of summons upon the defendant/opposite-party, as the case may be, the onus is upon the plaintiff/petitioner that the summons of the suit or the case was served upon the defendant/opposite-party. Moreover Order V, rule 12 of the Code has provided that whenever it is practicable, service of summons shall be made upon the defendant herein opposite-party in person unless he has an agent empowered to accept the service, in which case service on such agent shall be sufficient. Therefore this Court sitting on a revisional jurisdiction without any important question of law cannot interfere into such reasonable findings of the courts below.</u>

14. Having gone through the materials on record and particularly the provisions of service of summons upon the defendant in a suit, I am not inclined to interfere with the concurrent finding of the courts below.

15. With regard to the decision as referred to by the learned advocate for the petitioner, I find the same not applicable in context of the present facts and circumstances of the case and accordingly the same is not discussed.

16. In the result, the Rule is discharged.

17. Since the original suit was filed in the year 2007, the Court concerned is directed to dispose of the suit with utmost expedition preferably within 6 (six) months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

18. The order of stay and status quo at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby recalled and vacated.

Let a copy of this judgment be sent to the court concerned at once.

End.
