full_judgment:
Ahmed Sohel J: This First Miscellaneous Appeal filed by the appellant, Islami Bank Bangladesh Limited is directed against the impugned order No. 10 dated 6-1-2012, under section 19(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, passed by the learned Judge Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 2012 arising out of Artha Rin Suit No. 619 of 2008 allowing the Miscellaneous Case and thereby setting aside the ex-parte judgment and decree dated 22-3-2009 passed in Artha Rin Suit No. 619 of 2008.

2. Facts necessary for disposal of the Appeal, in short, is that the present appellants as plaintiffs filed Artha Rin Suit No. 619 of 2008 in the Court of Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka (hereinafter referred to as Adalat) against the respondents praying for a decree for recovery of outstanding loan of Taka 1,72,22461.

3. The defendants of the Artha Rin Suit did not appear and contested the suit although summons were duly served upon them as per the report of the process server.

4. The learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat fixed the date on 22-3-2009 for ex-parte hearing of the Artha Rin Suit and on that date passed the ex-parte judgment and decree against the defendants which was drawn on 25-3-2009.

5. In pursuant to the ex-parte decree the appellant as decree-holder filed application for execution before the Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka describing in the schedule both immovable property and cargo vessel to be sold in execution for realization of decreetal sum and was registered as Artha Jari Case No. 106 of 2009 and in due compliance of law got a certificate in its favour under section 33(5) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003.

6. The decree-holder Bank published auction notice in the 'Daily Songram' and `Dainik Amar Desh' to sell the mortgaged property fixing 13-4-2011 as the date of Auction. The Auction took place on the above date after completing all the formalities, delivery of possession of the Auction sold properties including the cargo vessel was completed and the decree-holder appellant Bank received the auction price in accordance with law.

7. That on 11-1-2012 the present respondents, the defendants of Artha Rin Suit No. 619 of 2008 filed a Miscellaneous case No. 1 of 2012, under section 19(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 before the Adalat Dhaka for setting aside the ex-parte judgment and decree dated 22-3-2009 (decree signed on 25-3-2009) and also prayed for restoration of the suit to its original file and number stating inter alia that summons were not served upon them properly and that they knew nothing about the suit as well as the decree until 1-1-2012.

8. The respondents of the present First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 105 of 2012 without serving any summons or notice or any copy of the said application upon the appellant, (plaintiff of the Artha Rin Suit) the learned Judge, of the Artha Rin Adalat after hearing the defendant only, pleased to allow the Miscellaneous Case on 16-1-2012 by setting aside the ex-parte decree dated 22-3-2009 and restored the Artha Rin Suit No. 619 of 2008 to its original file and number.

9. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid impugned order No. 10 dated 16-1-2012 of the Adalat, the plaintiffs as appellants preferred this Miscellaneous Appeal before this Court with an application for stay operation of the impugned order dated 16-1-2012 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka, upon which this Court by the order dated 27-2-2012 issued Rule and stayed all further proceedings of Artha Rin Suit No. 619 of 2008 for 3 (three) months and later on the said stay has been extended till disposal of the Rule. The Rule was registered as Civil Rule No. 164 (FM) of 2012.

10. Mr Ahsanul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing with Mr Khairul Alam Choudhury, Mr Md Kabir Iqbal Hossain and Ms. Farzana Khan, learned Advocates on behalf of the appellants at the very outset submits that the Artha Rin Adalat committed serious error in law in allowing the miscellaneous case in particular that the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat failed to consider that no notice and copy of the application under section 19(2) of the Ain was served upon the plaintiffs-appellants before taking up the said application for disposal.

11. He further submits that the learned Judge, failed to discuss as to how the defendant respondents came to the finding about the knowledge of the respondents about the ex-parte order dated 22-3-2009, decree signed on 25-3-2009 passed in Artha Rin Suit No. 619 of 2008 without considering any evidence in respect of limitation. In this respect he has drawn out attention to Annexure-F of the application for stay filed by the appellant, from where it is found that the defendant-respondents were very much aware of the decree passed ex-parte in Artha Rin Suit No. 619 of 2008 as far back as at least in 2009 as it is evident that an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure had been filed before the Hon'ble High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 19420 of 2009 (wherein the present respondents had annexed the ex-parte decree dated 22-3-2009 (decree signed on 25-3-2009) as Annexure-E in their application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure) which clearly proves that they were well aware of the said ex-parte decree at least in 2009. The respondents claim that they knew nothing about the suit as well as the decree until 1-1-2012 was not correct at all. Therefore, the date of knowledge is clearly more than 30 (thirty) days before filing of the application under section 19(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat 2003, which is hopelessly barred by special law of limitation laid down in section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003.

12. He next submits that without ascertaining the question of limitation, the learned Judge, having satisfied himself of compliance of only one requirement of deposit of 10% of the decreetal amount erroneously allowed the Miscellaneous Case without satisfying himself that the said application was not indeed filed within 30 days from the date of knowledge of the defendant-respondents and as such the impugned order is not sustainable in the eye of law and required to be set aside.

13. In support of his submissions, he referred 2 (two) decisions, Bangladesh Development Bank Ltd vs Judge Artha Rin Adalat, Jessore reported in 66 DLR 1; and Pubali Bank Ltd vs Bangladesh reported in 66 DLR 317.

14. Furthermore, he submits that the suppression of facts amounts to fraud upon the Court and fraud vitiates everything and he is not entitled to get any relief due to this suppression of facts. Accordingly, he prayed for allowing the Appeal.

15. On the other hand, Mr Md Reza-e-Murshed Kamal, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents by filing an affidavit-in-opposition and Counter-Affidavit, contesting the Appeal and submits that the facts of the case of the respondent opposite parties No. 1 to 3 are that they never applied for any loan in the said Bank rather one Mahbubur Rahman a Bank staff misguided the respondent opposite-parties and provoked them to apply for loan.

16. He next submits that the present respondents did not know about the judgment and decree passed by the 4th Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka in Artha Rin Suit No. 619 of 2008. The respondents came to know firstly from the Criminal Case No. 1089 of 2011 filed by the Bank in the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Dhaka under section 419/420/465/ 467/471/109 of the Penal Code. Wherein an application dated 1-1-2012 has been filed for 'shown arrest' the accused petitioner and in that application, the number of Artha Rin Execution Case No. 47 of 2011 has been written. Thereafter after knowing about the said ex-parte order passed in Artha Rin Suit No. 619 of 2008, the present respondents filed a Miscellaneous Case No. 01 of 2012 before the Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka under section 19(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 for restoration of the original Artha Rin Suit No. 619 of 2008 and the same was allowed and restored the said suit. However the said suit is now stayed by the order of the Hon'ble High Court Division in

Civil Rule No. 164 (FM) of 2012 filed by the appellants.

17. He further submits that the Artha Rin Suit No. 619 of 2008 is totally false, manufactured and the defendants No. 1 to 3 are not responsible for the outstanding dues as demanded by the plaintiffs bank and is not entitled to get any relief as prayed for and the order of stay passed by the Hon'ble High Court Division in this Civil Rule is liable to be vacated for the ends of justice.

18. At the time of hearing, the learned Advocate for the respondents was confronted with the question of date of knowledge of the ex-parte decree dated 22-3-2009 in particular the application filed by the respondents under section 561A of Code of Criminal Procedure i.e. regarding Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 19420 of 2009, wherein the respondents annexed the certified copy of the judgment of the ex-parte decree dated 22-3-2009 (decree signed on 25-3-2009) that the respondents had knowledge of the ex-parte decree at least in the year of 2009 and this suppression of fact, amounts to committing fraud upon the Court. In reply the learned Counsel for the respondents finding himself in difficult position to address the point confronted with and could not give any satisfactory reply to this point of suppression of facts rather admitted it. However, he finally submits that for the ends of justice, the respondents should be given a last chance to contest the suit.

19. We have heard the learned Advocates of both the parties with profound attention, perused the impugned order of the Adalat and the papers and documents as available on the record and the decisions of our apex Court very carefully.

20. Now, for the convenience of under-standing section 19 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is quoted below:

“১৯। (১) মামলার শুনানীর জন্য ধার্য্য কোন তারিখে বিবাদী আদালতে অনুপস্থিত থাকিলে, কিংবা মামলা শুনানীর জন্য গৃহীত হইবার পর ডাকিয়া বিবাদীকে উপস্থিত পাওয়া না গেলে, আদালত মামলা একতরফা সূত্রে নিষ্পত্তি করিবে।

(২) কোন মামলা একতরফা সূত্রে ডিক্রী হইলে, বিবাদী উক্ত একতরফা ডিক্রীর তারিখে অথবা উক্ত একতরফা ডিক্রী সম্পর্কে অবগত হইবার ৩০ (ত্রিশ) দিবসের মধ্যে, উপ-ধারা (৩) এর

বিধান সাপেক্ষে, উক্ত একতরফা ডিক্রী রদের জন্য দরখাস্ত করিতে পারিবেন।

(৩) উপ-ধারা (২) এর বিধান অনুযায়ী দরখাস্ত দাখিলের ক্ষেত্রে বিবাদীকে উক্ত দরখাস্ত দাখিলের তারিখের পরবর্তী ১৫ (পনের) দিবসের মধ্যে ডিক্রীকৃত অর্থের ১০% এর সমপরিমাণ

টাকা বাদীর দাবীর সেই পরিমাণের জন্য স্বীকৃতিস্বরূপ নগদ সংশ্লিষ্ট আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানে, অথবা জামানতস্বরূপ ব্যাংক ড্রাফট, পে-অডার বা অন্য কোন প্রকার নগদায়নযোগ্য বিনিময়ে দলিল

(Negotiable Instrument) আকারে জামানত হিসাব আদালতে জমাদান করিতে হইবে।

(8) উপ-ধারা (৩) এর বিধানমতে ডিক্রীকৃত অর্থের ১০% এর সমপরিমান টাকা জমাদানের সংগে সংগে দরখাস্তটি মঞ্জুর হইবে, এরতরফা ডিক্রী রদ হইবে এবং মূল মামলা উহার পূর্বের নম্বর ও নথিতে পুনরুজ্জীবিত হইবে, এবং আদালত এ মর্মে একটি আদেশ লিপিবদ্ধ করিবে, এবং অতঃপর মামলাটি যে পর্যায়ে একতরফা নিষ্পত্তি হইয়াছিল, এ পর্যায়ের অব্যবহিত পূর্ববর্তী পর্যায় হইতে পরিচালিত হইবে ।

(৫) বিবাদী উপ-ধারা (৩) বিধানমতে ডিক্রীকৃত অর্থের ১০% এর সমপরিমাণ টাকা বাদীর সেই পরিমাণের জন্য স্বীকৃতিস্বরূপ নগদ সংশ্লিষ্ট আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান, অথবা জামানতস্বরপ ব্যাংক ড্রাফট, পে-অর্ডার বা অন্য কোন প্রকার নগদায়নযোগ্য বিনিময়ে দলিল (Negotiable Instrument) আকারে জামানত হিসাব আদালতে জমাদান করিতে ব্যর্থ হইলে, উক্ত দরখাস্তটি সরাসরি খারিজ হইবে, এবং আদালত এ মর্মে একটি আদেশ লিপিবদ্ধ করিবে।

(৬) অর্থ ঋণ আদালতে বিচারাধীন কোন মামলা, বাদীর অনুপস্থিতির বা ব্যর্থতা হেতু খারিজ করা যাইবে না, এবং এইরূপ ক্ষেত্রে আদালত, নথিতে উপস্থাপিত কাগজাদি পরীক্ষা করিয়া গুনাগুন বিশ্লেষণে মামলা নিস্পত্তি করিবে।”

21. From the combined reading of the above provisions, it appears that Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 gives a clear understanding that right after passing of the ex-parte decree or from the date of knowledge of the ex-parte decree if within 30 days as per sub-section (3) of section 19 by depositing 10% of the decreetal amount an application has been filed for restoration of the suit after setting aside the ex-parte decree, the suit will be automatically restored in terms of section 19(4) of the Ain to its original file and number.

22. Further, two aspects have been made clear in the said provisions of law that an application for restoration of the suit after setting-aside ex-parte decree may be made within 30 days right after passing of the ex-parte decree or from the date of knowledge of the ex-parte decree. The words used in sub-section 2 of section 19 of Ain “একতরফা ডিক্রির তারিখের অথবা উক্ত

একতরফা ডিক্রি সম্পর্কে অবগত হইবার ৩০ দিবসের মধ্যে, উপ-ধারা(৩) এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে উক্ত এক তরফা ডিক্রী রদের জন্য দরখাস্ত করিতে পারিবেন” clearly indicates two different situations for filing an application for restoration.

23. Firstly, right after passing of the ex-parte decree and secondly, from the date of knowledge of the ex-parte decree as the case may be.

24. Now, the question comes to our mind that whether by implication of sub-section 4 of section 19 of the Ain, the suit will be automatically restored in both the situations.

25. It is clear from the plain reading of the above provisions of law that right after passing of the ex-parte decree, section 19(4) of the Ain comes into play i.e. the application if so filed within 30 days shall be automatically restored.

26. However, it does not apply in a case where it has been contended by the defendant that having knowledge of the ex-parte decree the application for restoration has been filed.

27. Now, it is our view that when the question of knowledge is the basis for deciding an application for restoration that should be decided after taking evidence and hearing both the parties.

28. Furthermore, it has been decided in the case of Pubali Bank Ltd. vs Bangladesh reported in 66 DLR 317 that

"section 19(2) of the Ain does not expressly prescribe for issuance of any notice upon the decree-holder to show cause in determining the correctness of the date of knowledge but it is the established principle of law that even when a statute is silent, notice has to be given if any person is sought to be affected in his right, interest, property or character".

29. Similar view has been expressed in the Indian Jurisdiction in the Case of Maneka Gandhi vs Union of India reported in AIR 1978 (SC) 597.

30. It is our considered view that after pronouncement of ex-parte decree a legal right has been accrued in favour of the plaintiff (decree-holder) and allowing of an application for setting aside the said decree, is curtailing the accrued right of the decree-holder.

31. In such a situation, our opinion is that the plaintiff has got a right to be informed about hearing of the said application by proper notice and the Adalat after hearing both the parties shall decide the issue as to correctness of the defendants alleged date of knowledge in order to satisfy itself towards the compliance of section 19(2) of the AM. In the instant case the Adalat did not comply with the said procedure of law.

32. Now, in the present case, the ex-parte judgment and decree was passed on 22-3-2009 and as per section 19(2) of the Ain requires the defendant to file an application for setting aside the ex-parte decree either within 30 days from the date of passing of the said decree or within 30 days from the date of knowledge, about the said ex-parte decree.

33. Admittedly, it is found from the materials available on record that the respondents were very much aware of the ex-parte decree dated 22-3-2009 in Artha Rin Suit No. 619 of 2008 as far back as at least in the year 2009 contrary to their claim of date of knowledge that they knew nothing about the suit as well as the decree until 1-1-2012, which is abundantly clear that it is suppression of fact and amounts to fraud upon the court. In the present case, the defendant filed the Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 2012 on 11-1-2012 which is clearly beyond 30 days of passing the ex-parte decree dated 22-3-2009.

34. It appears from the impugned order dated 16-1-2012 that the learned Judge of the Adalat, only consider one requirement of section 19 of the Ain of depositing of 10% decreetal amount by the defendant but did not at all consider anything regarding the question of limitation i.e. whether the case is filed within 30 days from the date of knowledge.

<u>35. Furthermore, as per section 3 of the Limitation Act, 1908, which confers a duty upon the Court to see as to whether the suit/application is filed within time or not even if the issue of limitation has not been pressed, the court is legally bound to see and decide such issue in disposing of the matter before it.</u>

<u>36. Now, the law is well settled that under a Special law where a time limit has been given to file an appeal, the provision of section 5 of limitation Act will not apply and the Artha Rin Adalat AM 2003, being a special law, the provisions of section 5 of the limitation Act will not apply and therefore the application for restoration shall be rejected outright.</u>

37. Further, 'he who comes into equity must come with clean hands'. It operates to prevent any affirmative recovery for the person with 'unclean hands' no matters how unfairly, the person’s adversary has treated him or her. The maxim is the basis of the clean hands doctrine. Its purpose is to protect the integrity of the Court.

38. In the present facts and circumstances of the case, we hold that the petitioners (respondents herein) of the Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 2012 have come up with unclean hands.

39. In the Pase of Zillur Rahman (Md) vs Md Abdul Quiyum Sarker reported in 18 BLC (AD) 258 it has been that

"Fraud vitiates everything. The plaintiff successed to prove that fraud was practised upon him by the defendant in executing and registering the impugned deed, it vitiated the entire transaction."

40. Further it has been held in the case of Janata Insurance Company Ltd vs Commissioner, Customs, Excise and VAT, Dhaka reported in 18 BLC 562 that "The suppression of fact is a heinous, detestable act, which cuts the very root of any claim made in any discipline, far less to say before Constitutional Court. Therefore, caution goes without any controversy that suppression of fact vitiates everything."

41. It is to be borne in mind that fraud or suppression of fact and fair play cannot dwell together, one must exclude the other. The Court stands for fair play only and to get equitable relief the respondent must approach the Court with clean hands.

42. It is settled legal proposition, decided in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd vs. Rajendra Singh AIR 2000 SC 1165, wherein the Hon'ble Court observed that "Fraud and Justice never dwell together" and it is a pristine maxim which has never lost its temper over all these centuries.

<u>43. It is our considered view that an act of fraud on Court is always viewed seriously. In Judicial proceedings, once fraud is proved, all advantages gained by playing fraud can be taken away. Suppression of any material fact/document amounts to a fraud upon the court.</u>

<u>44. When facts are intentionally misrepresented or where a false statement is made intentionally, with the knowledge that it is false, with a view to deceive the other party, it is known as fraud. In the present case, it is clear that the respondents had knowledge of the ex-parte decree at least in the year of 2009, which is clearly suppression of facts and amounts to committing fraud upon the Court.</u>

45. Further, in the English Jurisdiction, in general, fraud has been defined as 'Fraud includes the suppression of the truth as well as the presentation of false information.' Any attempt to deceive is considered fraud, and when the attempt to deceive occurs in a judicial proceeding, it is "fraud upon the Court."

46. From the above discussions, it is crystal clear that the Adalat has committed wrong in passing the impugned order dated 16-1-2012 without deciding the question of limitation, which is a non speaking order and erroneous and should be interfered with as fraud has been committed upon the court. Thus we find merit in the appeal.

47. In the result, the appeal is allowed without any order as to cost. The impugned order No. 10 dated 16-1-2012 passed by the learned Judge, Artha Ain Adalat, 4th Court, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 2012 arising out of Artha Rin Suit No. 619 of 2008 is hereby set aside. Consequently, the connected Civil Rule No. 164 (FM) of 2012 is made absolute.

Communicate the judgment and order to the concerned Adalat for taking necessary steps.

End.

full_judgment:
Rule was issued in the instant Civil Revisional application calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 18-5-2016 passed by the learned District Judge, Khagrachari Hill District in Civil Appeal No. 8 of 2011 affirming the impugned judgment and decree dated 3-3-2011 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Khagrachari Hill District in Civil Case No. 45 of 2008 decreeing the case should not be set aside and or pass such other order or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. The respondent as plaintiff filed Civil Suit No. 45 of 2008 in the court of learned Joint District Judge, Khagrachari Hill District for declaration of title in the suit and with prayer for evicting the defendant and with further prayer for restoration. The court of learned Joint District Judge, Khagrachari Hill District after hearing both sides allowed and decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff by its judgment and decree dated 3-3-2011. Against the judgment and decree dated 3-3-2011 passed by the trial court the defendant in the suit being the instant petitioner here as appellant filed Civil Appeal No. 8 of 2011 in the court of learned District Judge, Khagrachari Hill District. After hearing the learned District Judge, Khagrachari Hill District dismissed the appeal by its judgment and decree dated 18-5-2016 and thereby affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial court dated 3-3-2011.

3. Being dissatisfied and aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the appellate court the defendant-appellant as petitioner filed the instant Civil Revisional application which is presently before this court for disposal.

4. The case of the plaintiff inter alia is that the land mentioned in the schedule of plaint originally belonged to Mongshe Mogh appertaining to Khatian No. 290 of Golabari Mouza being Plot No. 4332 measuring 47 decimals of land and that the land in question was purchased by the plaintiff by starting mutation case No. 33 of 1999 which was approved by the Deputy Commissioner, Khagrachari on 27-12-1999. Since then the plaintiff was in possession of the suit land upon paying rent year to year to the Government. All on a sudden the defendant forcibly entered the suit land on 22-12-2007 and dispossessed the plaintiff from 37 decimals of land out of 47 decimals. Thereafter, defendant planted banana garden on 37 decimals of land. Having heard the news the plaintiff asked the defendant in presence of local pourashava commissioner to handover the possession of 37 decimals of land to the petitioner. The defendant did not pay heed to any word of the plaintiff. Hence, the plaintiff filed this case against the petitioner for restoration of possession and declaration of title in the suit land.

5. The defendant opposite party contested the suit by filing written statement alleging inter alia that the land in question is not identical and the suit is barred by limitation and not maintainable in the eye of law and the plaintiff have no cause of action in filing this suit. The defendant have been living with his family on the suit land by constructing hut. The suit land would be valued at about Taka 2,00,000 (Two lac) only but there is no valuation of land. The defendant acquired the suit land by way of settlement. And hence the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost.

6. Learned Advocate Mr Md Shahidullah Bhuiyan, Advocate appeared for the petitioner while learned Advocate Mr Md Zishan Mahmud along with Ms. Tanzila Ferdouse, learned Advocates represented the opposite party.

7. Learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that both the courts below upon error of law and fact gave findings in favour of the plaintiff (the present opposite party) and therefore both the judgment of the courts below ought to be set aside for ends of justice. He contends that the suit is not maintainable in the first instance. By way of elaborating his contention that the suit is not maintainable he submits that till the year 2003 the Administration of Justice in the Chittagong Hill Tracts where the suit land is situated was conducted and administered by the concerned Deputy Commissioner. He continues that prior to 2003 there were no civil courts in the Chittagong Hill Tracts and the rules and laws under the Civil Procedure, 1908 therefore was not applicable. He further continues that however in the year 2003, the Chittagong Hill Tracts Regulation, 1900 (regulation No.1 of 1900) was amended by Ain No. 38 of 2003 and contends that by way of such amendment the previous rules of civil justice which was administrated by the concerned Deputy Commissioner was replaced and amended. He submits that it was inserted in the Amendment of 2003 that the concerned Districts of Chittagong Hill Tracts shall constitute three separate sessions divisions and the concerned District Judge shall be the Sessions Judge of the respective sessions division and the Joint District Judge shall be the Assistant Sessions Judge. In this context he presses that pursuant to the amendment of 2003 the Administration of Justice was transferred and conferred to the Civil court as in the rest of the country and the applicable rules and laws and provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908 and all other relevant and ancillary laws relating thereto became applicable to any case or suit which may be filed regarding any land whatsoever situated in the Chittagong Hill Tracts. He points out that the instant suit was filed in the year 2008 and therefore the amended law of 2003 is applicable in the present case. In this context he further submits that under the amended law all the other rules and laws related thereto became applicable to a suit filed in any case filed in any court in the Chittagong Hill Tracts including the Court-fees Act of 1870. He draws this court's attention to the fact that however at the stage of filing of the present suit the requisite court-fees was not paid by the plaintiff and Court Fee is payable under the Court-fees Act, 1870 and therefore the suit is not maintainable being barred by law. He agitated that both the courts below overlooked this significant factor that due to non-payment of the Courts Fees under the Court-fees Act, 1870 the suit filed in limine is not maintainable. He further continues that the courts below also made errors of law given that the trial court gave an order to have the suit land measured by a local surveyor and did not follow the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 which provides for investigation into the property by appointing an Advocate Commissioner under Order XXVI, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908. He asserts that under the amended Rules of 2003, all the provisions of Code of Civil Procedure including that of the provision of appointment of the Advocate Commissioner for investigation into the suit land in the event of necessity to ascertain and determine any dispute or issues pertaining to the suit land shall henceforth pursuant to amendment of 2003 be applicable in any case arising out of any land which is a subject of dispute in the Chittagong Hill Tracts. He argues that necessary provisions of law under the Courts Fees Act, 1870 and Order XXVI, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure not being followed therefore the judgment of the courts below are not sustainable and also given that there are both factual and legal errors in the judgments and therefore both judgment of the courts below ought to be set aside and the Rule bears merit and ought to be made absolute for ends of justice.

8. Learned Advocate for the opposite party submits that both the courts below upon correctly considering evidences and upon correct interpretation thereof arrived upon their concurrent findings. He argues that in the absence of misreading of evidences and finding of fact the judgment of the courts below need not be interfered with. Controverting the argument of the petitioner regarding non payment of court-fees under the Court-fees Act, 1870 and non compliance of Order XXVI, rule 9 of the CPC 1908, the learned Advocate for the opposite party submits that the petitioner cannot raise such an argument at this stage since he did not raise this issue during Trial and or Appeal before the concerned Courts. He submits that the courts below did not commit any illegality as such and therefore the Rule does not bear merit and ought to be discharged for ends of justice.

9. I have heard the learned Advocates from both sides, perused the application and materials-on-records before me and I have examined the relevant laws. It appears upon examination into the records that truly the requisite court-fees payable under the Court-fees Act, 1870 was not paid during filing of the suit. Upon a query from the court the learned Deputy Attorney-General Mr Abdus Salam Mondal along with Mrs. Shahida Khatoon, learned Assistant Attorney-General both being present in court submits that pursuant to the amended law of 2003 subsequently the Code of Civil Procedure and other laws relating to Civil suits is also applicable to any case filed in the Civil Courts in the Chittagong Hill Tracts. He submits that therefore Court-fees Act, 1870 shall be applicable and payable in the present suit. Upon a further query from the court the learned DAG and AAG submits that since it appears that the courts fees remained unpaid not due to any deliberate lacuna on the part of the plaintiff therefore for ends of justice this court sitting in revision can through exercising its revisional powers give an appropriate direction that the plaintiff in the original suit (the opposite party here) shall pay the requisite Court Fee prospectively to the concerned trial court and this court may also issue further direction that the concerned court may accept the court-fees prospectively upon following the provisions in the rules under the Court-fees Act, 1870.

10. I have examined the records of the case and it appears from the record that in this case non-payment of the Court-Fees at the stage of filing of the suit was not due to any deliberate apathy or lacuna on the part of the plaintiff. It was the duty of the concerned courts below to ascertain and ensure that requisite proper court-fees was paid during filing of the suit under the Court-fees Act, 1870. Strangely enough both the courts below overlooked this significant fact. I am of the considered opinion that due to non exercise of due diligence by the concerned courts even though in all probabilities inadvertently, however the plaintiff must not suffer since the non-payment is not due to any fault of the plaintiff. I find force in the submission of the learned DAG along with learned AAG that this court while exercising revisional jurisdiction under section 115(1) the Code of Civil Procedure 1908 read along with section 151 of the Code, may in an appropriate case issue such direction as it thinks fit for ends of justice.

11. I have looked into the Amendment of 2003 vide Ain No. 38 of 2003 of the Chittagong Hill Tracts Regulation, 1900 (Regulation 1 of 1900) এর অধিকতর সংশোধনকল্পে প্রনীত আইন which is published by Gazette Notification on September, 2003. The relevant portion was amended as such:

8 Regulation No. 1 of 1990 এর section 8 এর সংশোধন। উক্ত Regulation এর section 8 এর-

(ক)(sub-section) (1) এর পরিবর্তে নিম্নরুপ sub-section (1)প্রতিস্থাপিত হইবে, যথাঃ-

(1) The Rangamati, Khagrachory and Bandarban districts of the Chittagong Hill Tracts shall constitute three separate sessions divisions and the concerned District Judge shall be the Sessions Judge of the respective sessions division and the Joint District Judge shall be the Assistant Sessions Judge.";

(খ) sub-section (2) এর-

(অ)প্রথম লাইনের "A" শব্দের পরিবর্তে "The"শব্দটি প্রতিস্থাপিত হইবে এবং "the commissioner" শব্দগুলি বিলুপ্ত হইবে এবং

(আ) ষষ্ট লাইনের "warrant—শব্দটিও ড্যাস চিহ্নটি বিলুপ্ত হইবে,

(গ) sub-section (2)  এরপর নিম্নরুপ sub-section (3), (4) এবং (5) সংযোজিত হইবে, যথাঃ-

"(3) The Rangamati, Khagrachory and Bandarban districts of the Chittagong Hill Tracts shall constitute three separate jurisdictions under three District Judges.

(4) The Joint District Judge as a court of original jurisdiction, shall try all civil cases in accordance with the existing laws, customs and usages of the districts concerned, except the cases arising out of the family laws and other customary laws of the tribes of the districts of Rangamati, Khagrachory and Bandarban respectively which shall be triable by the Mauza Headmen and Circle Chiefs.

(5) An appeal against the order, judgment and decree of the joint District Judge shall lie to the District Judge."

12. It is obvious that this amended version inserted by the Ain No. 38 of 2003 is preceded by the previous Rules followed in the arena of the administration of justice relating to matters and cases of Civil nature in the concerned districts in Chittagong Hill Tracts.

Rule 4(খ) (2)(অ) reads:

(অ)প্রথম লাইনের "As" শব্দের পরিবর্তে 'The" শব্দটি প্রতিস্থাপিত হইবে এবং "the commissioner" শব্দগুলি বিলুপ্ত হইবে,

<u>13. This amendment and বিলুপ্ত ’ clearly express that previously the civil judicial functions was administered by the Commissioner or Deputy Commissioner and not by Judges in the Civil Courts. It is also clear enough that Code of Civil Procedure and the other related laws for example the Court-fees Act, 1870 was not followed in Civil Suits in the Hill Tracts prior to the Amendment of 2003. It is evident that the applicability of mandatory payment of court-fees during filing of Civil Suits came into effect pursuant to the Gazette Notification on September 21st, 2003. Prior to 2003, the administration of justice in the Chittagong Hill Tracts was conducted and administered by the Deputy Commissioner whatsoever adhering to the local customs and tradition and a different set of Rules were followed in any suits of Civil nature which were filed in the Chittagong Hill Tracts.</u>

14. It goes without saying that this particular region and the society therein since eons before adhered to and have been governed by their local customs, Rules and tradition.

15. Chittagong Hill Tracts Regulations, 1900 was amended as late as in 2003 and pursuantly that particular region became subject to the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 and other related Laws and Rules became applicable to the civil cases in Civil Courts in general. The previous old Rule of no provision and non-requirement of payment of court-fees in any case in the Chittagong Hill Tracts is reflected in the RULES FOR THE ADMINISTRATION OF CHITTAGONG HILL TRACTS in Chittagong Hill Tracts Regulation, 1900.The relevant Rule is expressed in Rule 4 of the Regulation of 1900 which is reproduced below:-

4. No court-fees shall be payable on a memorandum of appeal in case where a Chakma, Mogh or member of any tribe indigenous to the Hill Tracts the appellant.

<u>16. Such being the position of the law prior to the amendment of 2003, it is necessary to be reminded that for the concerned officials and others concerned to be well informed of the new set of Rules needs time. It can be reasonably presumed that the inhabitants of that region and the officers, employees and other persons dealing with matters related to judicial administration were not aware or otherwise conversant with all the Rules applicable to Civil Courts including the applicability of the provisions of Court-fees Act 1870 which were introduced in the administration of civil justice pursuant to the amendment of 2003.</u>

<u>17. As a general rule, court-fees must be paid at the time of institution of a suit following the provisions of the Act of 1870. Yet this particular case in my opinion is an exceptional case, arising out of a particular circumstance and for ends of justice I am inclined to set it apart from the general rule. Therefore, I am of the considered opinion that failure to pay the court-fees during filing of the suit in this particular case arose out of a special circumstance, in all probabilities due to lack of knowledge and ignorance of the concerned officials and others regarding the relatively recent Amended Laws of 2003. Hence, I am of the considered opinion that this is a fit case wherein the plaintiff ought to be allowed to pay the requisite courts fees under the Court-fees Act, 1870 prospectively.</u>

18. The learned Advocate for the petitioner argues that the trial court did not follow the provisions of Order XXVI, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure by not calling for appointing an Advocate Commissioner under Order XXVI, rule 9 of the Code, rather it gave order to get the land measured by a local surveyor. Controverting this argument of the petitioner, the Learned Advocate for the opposite party submitted that the petitioner cannot at this stage of the case make such argument given that the defendant petitioner neither during the suit nor during appeal raised any objection nor did they make any application before the court to have the suit land measured following the provisions of Order XXVI, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure by appointing an Advocate Commissioner.

19. Upon examining the record I also do not find anything from the record which may indicate that the defendant petitioner here made any application for investigation and for measuring the suit land by an Advocate Commissioner under Order XXVI, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Therefore, I am in agreement with the learned Advocate for the opposite party and I am also of the considered view that in such circumstances the petitioner cannot raise this issue in revision.

20. I have gone through the judgment of the courts below; I do not find any inconsistency as such in their concurrent findings of fact. Therefore, I do not think there is any reason to interfere with the judgments of the courts below relating to the findings of fact.

21. Hence, I find no merit in the Rule.

22. In the result, the Rule is discharged with directions.

23. The plaintiff opposite party is hereby directed to pay the requisite courts fees before the concerned court within 30 days after receiving this judgment and order and L.C.R are sent below and the concerned court is hereby directed to accept the court-fees relating to the Civil Suit No. 45 of 2008 in the court of learned Joint District Judge, Khagrachari Hill District. In default in the event of non payment of the court-fees within the specified time, the original suit shall stand dismissed.

24. Send down the lower courts records at once.

Communicate the judgment at once.

End.

full_judgment:
AKM Abdul Hakim J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite-party No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned order No. 189 dated 13-4-2015 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Chittagong in Money Execution Case No. 3 of 1992 allowing an application directing the Sonali Bank, Court Hill Branch, Chittagong to give Taka 93,54,314.13 to the opposite-party No. 1 which was deposited with the said Bank as FDR No. 1027567 within 7 (seven) working days with interest should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. The present opposite party, Md Nurul Alam Chowdhury as plaintiff instituted Money Suit No. 123 of 1986 which was subsequently renumbered as Money Suit No. 9 of 1991 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Chittagong impleading the present petitioner as defendant No. 1, opposite-party No. 2 and opposite-party No. 3 Agrani Bank as defendant No. 3 for realisation of Taka 65,80,089 (sixty five lac, eighty thousand and eighty nine) which was decreed on contest against defendant No.1 and ex-parte against other defendants by the judgment and decree dated 31-7-1991. Thereafter the plaintiff opposite-party filed Money Execution Case No. 3 of 1992 praying for satisfying the decreetal amount which is now lying in Sonali Bank, Court Hill Branch, Chittagong as FDR in Civil Deposit Account No. 1027567. The judgment debtor/petitioner herein filed written objection in the said money execution case on 31-5-1992.

3. The case of the decree-holder-plaintiff-opposite-party No.2 is that the plaintiff sold palm oil to defendant No.1 Bibhuti Bhushan Talukder and the money in account having not paid plaintiff instituted the aforesaid suit which was decreed. It is stated that in the suit plaintiff filed application under Order XXXVIII, rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure for attachment of Palm Oil of defendant No. 1 before judgment and ad-interim order of attachment was passed and as per order of the court, the process server on 19-7-1986 attached the property in advance and handed over custody of the attached Palm Oil to the plaintiff. Defendant No.1 did not raised any objection. Agrani Bank, Khatunjonj Branch, defendant No.3 in the present suit filed Money Suit No. 91 of 1986 subsequently renumbered as Money Suit No. 22 of 2011 and finally renumbered as Money Suit No. 330 of 2014. Against the present defendant No.1 of the instant suit filed an application for re-attachment which was allowed on 1-6-1987 the court passed order to sell the attached property of Money Suit No. 123 of 1986 considering Palm Oil as perishable property and it was sold in auction and the sale price of Taka 1,01,93,921 (one crore, one lac, ninety three thousand nine hundred and twenty one) was deposited with Sonali Bank, Court Hill Branch, Chittagong as FDR in Civil Deposit Account No. 1027567. Agrani Bank although not a party, filed written statement in Money Suit No. 123 of 1986, ultimately did not contest. Subsequently, Money Suit No. 9 of 1991 that is earlier Money Suit No. 123 of 1986 was decreed on contest on 31-7-1991.

Plaintiff filed Money Execution Case No. 03 of 1992 for execution of the decree. On 31-5-1992 the judgment-debtor filed written objection in Money Execution Case No. 3 of 1992. The court after hearing by order dated 13-8-1992 rejected the objection, against which judgment-debtor did not proceed further.

4. On 3-6-1987 Agrani Bank, plaintiff of Money Suit No. 91 of 1986 filed an application for withdrawal of Taka 8,38,964.87 (eight lac, thirty eight thousand, nine hundred sixty four and eighty seven paisa) and the court allowed the same. Judgment-debtor-defendant No.1 on 9-6-1987 filed an application praying rejection of the application of the Agrani Bank. The court rejected the application filed by the judgment-debtor on 9-6-1987. Thereafter, Agrani Bank the plaintiff of Money Suit No. 91 of 1986 on 21-7-1987 applied for payment order accordingly the same was allowed on 27-1-1987 and Agrani Bank withdrawn the amount of its claim Taka 8,54,314.13 (eight lac fifty four thousand three hundred fourteen and thirteen paisa) still remain at civil deposit account which was transferred to FDR No. 1027567 at Sonali Bank Court Hill Branch and was fixed for five years. Agrani Bank appeared in Money Execution Case No. 03 of 1992 and filed Civil Revision No. 2400 of 1992 against the order No. 7 dated 13-8-1992 before the High Court Division and High Court Division by order dated 18-7-1994 disposed of the revisional application allowing Agrani Bank to file his statement as defendant No.3 in the instant Execution Case. After order passed by the High Court Division Agrani Bank did not file any statement, thereafter the executing court by order No.22 directed to proceed with the execution case. After one year of the order passed by the High Court Division, Agrani Bank filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure with some false statement and prayed for deleting the schedule given in the execution application against which decree-holder on 13-7-1995 filed written objection. The court by order No. 32 dated 11-11-1995 rejected the application. Against which, Agrani Bank filed Civil Revision No. 4822 of 1995 before the High Court Division and High Court Division by order dated 4-7-1996 disposed of the revision directing the trial court to proceed with the execution case in accordance with law. On 22-2-2010 the decree-holder filed application which was heard on 4-3-2010 and the court directed decree-holder to serve notice upon the judgment-debtor. Notice was served on 5-5-2010 and on 7-6-2010. The Sonali Bank Court-Hill Branch, submitted report after receiving the notice by Order No. 124 dated 12-7-2010, then court rejected the application of the decree-holder finding that no money is deposited in present suit although there is a FDR in the name of defendant No. 1.

5. Thereafter the present opposite-party decree-holder filed an application before executing court under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for a direction upon the Sonali Bank to pay him 93,54,314 including interest till date which is lying as FDR in Civil Deposit No. 1027567 within seven working days. The Joint District Judge, First Court, Chittagong by the impugned order dated 13-4-2015 allowed the said application directing the Sonali Bank to pay the amount of Taka 93,54,314 including interest till date which is now lying in Sonali Bank, Court Hill Branch, Chittagong as FDR in Civil Deposit No. 1027567 within seven working days.

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order dated 13-4-2015, the judgment-debtor moved this application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule and stay.

7. During pendency of the Rule opposite-party No. 1 Md Nurul Alam Chowdhury died and his legal heirs was substituted as opposite-party No. 1(a)-1(g) by order dated 6-9-2016.

8. The opposite-party No.1 decree-holder contested the Rule by filing counter-affidavit dated 12-5-2016, supplementary counter-affidavit dated 29-5-2017 and additional supplementary affidavit dated 15-10-2018. In the counter-affidavit and supplementary affidavit it is contended by the opposite-party that the decree-holder filed Money Execution Case No. 3 of 1992 on 19-2-1992 against which Bibhuti Bhusan Talukder the judgment-debtor, present petitioner herein filed written objection on 31-5-1992 in the said execution case same was rejected by the executing court by Order No. 7 dated 13-8-1992 on the ground that since section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not in force, so there is no scope/jurisdiction for the judgment-debtor to file written objection in the executing court. It is further stated that Agrani Bank filed Money Suit No. 91 of 1986, subsequently renumbered as Money Suit No. 22 of 2011 and now renumbered as Money Suit No. 330 of 2014 for recovery of money from the present judgment-debtor and others. In the said suit the present decree-holder, Mohammad Nurul Alam Chowdhury was not impleaded as party and in the said suit the plaintiff Agrani Bank filed an application under Order XXXVII, rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the said prayer was allowed by order dated 18-9-1996. Against the said order the present petitioner through his father in law filed FMA No. 333 of 1986 and some other persons also filed five Civil Revisions those were heard analogously on 10-12-1986. Thereafter FMA No. 333 of 1986 renumbered 218 of 1991 is dismissed and all the revision being Civil Revision Nos. 566, 586, 569, 617, 618 of 1986 and Civil Rule No. 77(FM) of 1986 are discharged. Subsequently, the High Court Division allowed the Review Petition by order dated 30-6-1993 and the First Commercial Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Chittagong in Money Suit No. 91 of 1986 is directed to transfer the said sale proceed which is now deposited as "civil deposit" in Chittagong Branch of the Bangladesh Bank to a convenient Branch of the Sonali Bank in Chittagong near the Chittagong Court Building as Fixed Deposit Receipt (FDR) with time limit of 5 (five) years so that the said deposit earns interest and "none of the parties in to be allowed to encash interest as well as the principal until the said Money Suit No. 91 of 1986 of the First Commercial Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Chittagong is finally decided including appeals etc. in accordance with the executing court final order".

9. Mr Mahbubey Alam with Mr Md Mozammel Hossain. the learned Advocates appeared on behalf of the defendant-petitioner. Mr Md Mozammel Hossain, learned Advocate vehemently submits that the decree-holder opposite-party herein without serving any copy of the application obtained the impugned order dated 13-4-2015. He further submits that since the decree was passed directing the petitioner to pay Taka 65,80,089 with 20% interest on that amount but the executing court passed an order to pay Taka 93,59,314.13 including interest which is beyond the decree and the executing court has no jurisdiction to go beyond the decree. He finally submits that the order dated 30-6-1993 passed by the High Court Division in FMA No. 333 of 1986 with other five revisions has not been challenged in the Appellate Division and, as such, the same order is still in force. Accordingly, learned Advocate prayed that the Rule should be made absolute.

10. Mr Mahbubey Alam, the learned Advocate appeared before this court on 21-10- 2018 for the petitioner and his only submission is that unless the judgment and order dated 30-6-1993 passed by the High Court Division in review of the judgment and order dated 10-12-1986 passed in FMA No. 333 of 1986/FMA No. 218 of 1991 with Civil Revision Nos. 566, 586, 569, 617, 618 of 1986 and Civil Rule No. 77(FM) of 1986 is vacated the judgment-debtor will be seriously prejudice. Thus on this count the impugned order dated 13-4-2015 passed by the learned Joint District Judge in Money Execution Case No. 3 of 1992 should be set aside.

11. On the other hand, Mr Sadananda Rana with Mr Ajoy Shankar Bhowmik, the learned Advocates appeared for the plaintiff-decree-holder opposite-party. Mr Sadananda Rana, the learned Advocate in reply to the submission made by the learned Advocate Mr Mahbubey Alam submits that in Civil Revision No. 3895 of 2010 Rule was made absolute by order dated 20-1-2011 and this question was not raised in the revision and against the said order Agrani Bank filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 918 of 2012 which was dismissed on 27-11-2014 and affirmed the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in the said Civil Revision.

12. We have heard the submissions of the learned Advocate of both the parties, perused the revisional application and the annexures annexed thereto supplementary-affidavit and counter-affidavit filed by the opposite party.

13. It appears that the decree-holder-present opposite-party got a decree against the judgment-debtor-petitioner passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, First Court, Chittagong in Money Suit No. 9 of 1991/Money Suit No. 123 of 1986. Then the decree-holder filed Money Execution Case No. 3 of 1992 against the judgment and decree dated 31-7-1991 to execute the said decree. In the execution case the decree-holder filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 13-4-2015, which was rejected by the impugned order.

14. It appears that in Civil Revision No. 3895 of 2010 the High Court Division by judgment and order dated 20-2-2011 directed the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Chittagong to dispose of Money Execution Case No. 3 of 1992 in accordance with law. Against the said order Agrani Bank filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 918 of 2012 which was dismissed on 27-11-2014 and affirmed the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in the Civil Revision. It further appears that in compliance of the order dated 27-11-2014 passed by the Appellate Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 918 of 2012 the executing court passed the impugned order and disposed the Money Execution Case No. 3 of 1992 with a direction upon the Sonali Bank, Court Hills Branch, Chittagong to pay an amount of Taka 93,54,314 including interest till date to the decree-holder, Nurul Alam Chowdhury from the FDR account in Civil Deposit No. 1027567 now lying in Sonali Bank, Court Hills Branch, Chittagong within 7 (seven) days from the receipt of the order. Against this order the present judgment-debtor filed this revisional application and obtained Rule and stay on 30-8-2015 on the ground that High Court Division passed order dated 30-6-1993 in FMA No. 333 of 1986/ renumbered 218 of 1991 with the five revisions being Civil Revision Nos. 566, 586, 569, 617, 618 of 1986 to the effect that none of the parties is to be allowed to encash interest as well as the principal until the said Money Suit No. 91 of 1986 is disposed of.

15. We have carefully examined the judgment and order dated 30-6-1993 passed by the High Court Division in review of the judgment and order dated 10.12.1986 passed in FMA No. 333 of 1986/FMA No. 218 of 1991 with Civil Revision Nos. 566, 586, 569, 617, 618 of 1986 and Civil Rule No. 77(FM) of 1986. It is evident that aforesaid FMA and Civil Revisions were preferred against the judgment and order dated 107 dated 10-9-1986 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, First Commercial Court, Chittagong in Money Suit No. 91 of 1986. It is further evident that the present decree-holder, Md Nurul Alam Chowdhury was not a party in Money Suit No. 91 of 1986. Thus, we find that the judgment passed in the FMA with other Civil Revisions is not binding upon the present opposite-party decree-holder of Money Execution Case No. 3 of 1992 which arises out of Money Suit No. 123 of 1986 renumbered as Money Suit No. 9 of 1991. Moreover, section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure has been omitted by the Civil Procedure Code, 1908 (Amendment) Ordinance (Ordinance No. XLVIII) of 1993.

<u>16. We further find that the judgment-debtor has no locus-standi to file the present revisional application because of the fact that in Civil Revision No. 3859 of 2010 filed by the present decree-holder against the judgment-debtor and others impugning the order No. 124 dated 12-7-2010 rejecting the decree-holder application under section 151 finding that no money was deposited in the present suit although there is an amount lying in Sonali Bank, Court Hills Branch, Chittagong as FDR in Civil Deposit Account No. 1027567. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute on 20-2-2011 and set aside the Order No. 124 dated 12-7-2010 and further directed to depose of Money Execution Case No. 3 of 1992 in accordance with law. Against the said judgment and order dated 20-2-2011 the present opposite-party No. 3 filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 918 of 2012 before the Appellate Division which was dismissed by order dated 27-11-2014 and affirmed the judgment dated 20-2-2011 passed in Civil Revision No. 3895 of 2010.</u>

17. In the light of the findings, we find no substance in this Rule. Accordingly, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs.

18. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby vacated.

Let a copy of the judgment be sent to the concerned court expeditiously.

End.

full_judgment:
This Rule was issued by this Court on 24-9-2003 upon an application filed by the petitioner under section 115(1) of the code of civil procedure against the impugned judgment and order dated 30-6-2003 passed by Joint District Judge, Second Court, Barguna in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 1 of 2003 allowing the appeal by reversing those dated 13-11-2002 passed by Senior Assistant Judge, Barguna Sadar in Miscellaneous Case No. 2 of 2001.

2. The relevant facts for disposal of the case, in a nutshell, are that the petitioner purchased the suit shop room measuring two decimals of land thereof from one Abdul Latif Khan, the father and father-in- law of both the opposite parties on 5-4-1998 by a registered sale deed at the cost of Taka 10,000 [ten thousand]. Having taken possession of the shop room the petitioner started getting prepared for extension of the shop while opposite party No.1, third son of the vendor, forcibly entered the suit room on 9-4-1998 at night and began to live therein along with opposite party No. 2. This incident was informed to the vendor and local elites who asked them to vacate the suit room to which opposite party No.1 gave an undertaking to vacate the same by 22-12-1998 or to pay an amount of Taka 18,000 as price of the shop room including cost of construction of the boundary wall. But the opposite parties neither paid the aforesaid money nor vacated the shop room, hence the suit.

3. Having received the summons of the Title Suit No. 60 of 1999, the opposite party No. 1 appeared through lawyer on 31-10-1999 and took several adjournments from 28-11-1999 to 1-2-2000 for filing written statement in the suit. Eventually, he did not file any written statement or took any steps on 29-2-2000 and the suit was decreed ex-parte on 25-4-2000.

4. Thereafter, opposite party No.1 presented Miscellaneous Case No. 2 of 2001 under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure stating that he came to know about the ex-parte decree on 1-1-2001 and the reasons shown by him is that he could not take step because of his ailment. In support of this plea he submitted some medical documents at the time of rendering evidence before the court below.

5. Upon hearing the parties, perusing the medical documents and evidence, the Senior Assistant Judge, Barguna by his order dated 13-11-2002 rejected the miscellaneous case. Against which the opposite party No. 1 preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 1 of 2003 before the learned District Judge, Barguna. Ultimately the said miscellaneous appeal was heard by the learned Joint District Judge and allowed the same setting aside the order of Senior Assistant Judge dated 13-11-2002. Hence, the instant Rule came into light at the instant of the petitioner.

6. Mr Khandakar Diliruzzaman, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner contends that the application under order IX Rule 13 filed by the opposite party No.1 was barred by limitation under Article 164 of the Limitation Act. Having found no cogent reason with regard to taking no steps by the opposite parties in the suit on the date fixed, the trial court rightly and lawfully dismissed the miscellaneous case but the Appellate Court below committed an error of law resulting in the decision occasioning failure of justice in setting aside the ex-parte decree, is liable to be set-aside. He further contends that the grounds taken by the petitioner in disposing the miscellaneous case were referred to the decision given by the Appellate Court merely allowing cost, is not enough to set-aside the decree which caused failure of justice and, as such, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set-aside.

7. None stands on behalf of the opposite parties although this matter has figured in the list for hearing.

8. Heard the submissions of learned Advocate for the petitioner, perused the application, judgments and orders of both the courts below and other connected documents wherefrom it transpires that a title suit was filed by the present petitioner as plaintiff for a decree of ejectment from semi pacca shop room. The opposite party No.1 as defendant No.1 appeared in the said title suit and took several adjournments for filing written statement. After a while he showed no interest to take steps on the dates fixed in the suit for filing written statement. The trial court had given him ample opportunities to contest the case by filing written statement but he failed to prevail such opportunity. Thereafter, the suit was decreed ex-parte on 25-4-2000. After a long time of the ex-parte decree he preferred a miscellaneous appeal before the learned Sessions Judge reasoning that he could not take proper steps due to his ailment by submitting medical certificates issued by the doctor who did not come forward to support the medical certificates issued by him. It has further revealed that the ex-parte decree was made on 25-4-2000 and the opposite party No.1 allegedly came to know about this ex-parte decree on 1-1-2001, around eight months he was silent in taking any steps against ex-parte decree by showing reasonable explanation. Even then he did not show anything about his engaged lawyer who ought to have informed him with regard to the ex-parte decree.

<u>9. Supporting inordinate delay of taking steps he failed to produce evidence in the miscellaneous case. It appears from the judgment of Appellate Court below that he had been suffering from fever which turned into ulcer and rheumatic diseases. Such diseases were not supposed to make him unable to proceed with the case brought against him by the present petitioner and he could have scope to proceed with the case by suffering from such diseases. Learned judge of the Appellate Court below before taking final decision mentioned that the opposite party having appeared the case took adjournments for filing written statement but subsequently why did not take any steps next day i.e on 29-2-2000. Such views he expressed are the grounds of the petitioner but he did not consider it in favour of the petitioner. Moreover, as per Article 164 of the Limitation Act, the application for setting aside the ex-parte decree was to be filed within thirty days to be counted from the date of judgment and decree or when the applicant has knowledge of the decree if failed there must be a proper explanation for condonation of delay under Limitation Act which was not rendered by the opposite party and he could not have any scope to say that he had no knowledge about the ex-parte decree because he entered appearance in the suit after getting summons from the trial court and he would not know the subsequent fixed dates, is fettered from truthfulness. It finds support from the case of Begum Meherunnessa vs Secretary, Ministry of Public Works and Urban Development, Dhaka, reported in 7 BLC 662 where it was held as under,</u>

<u>"Defendant-opposite parties appeared in the suit and took several adjournments for filing written statement and ultimately defendants did not take any steps as a result of which the suit was decreed ex parte. Defendants filed application under Order IX, rule 13, CPC which became time barred by 182 days. Under Article 164 of the Limitation Act, the period of limitation is 30 days for an order to set aside a decree passed ex parte. Since the defendant Government took several adjournments for filing written statement it is neither believable nor acceptable that the government pleader and the defendant would not know the subsequent fixed dates. Learned Additional District Judge neither passed any specific order for condonation of the delay nor did he allow the application for condonation of delay nor did he give any finding as to the sufficient cause for condoning the delay and hence the impugned judgment is set aside."</u>

10. Further claim of the opposite parties is that the summons issued by the trial court in the original suit, was not served upon the opposite party No. 2 as defendant No. 2 but it has emerged from the earlier discussion that the opposite party Nos.1 and 2 both used to live together in the occupied shop room as husband and wife. Opposite party No.1 having appeared in the suit took several adjournments for filing written statement whereas opposite party No. 2 being the wife of the opposite party No.1 did not have knowledge about the suit filed by the petitioner, is neither believable nor acceptable.

11. In the facts and circumstances discussed above, this court finds substance in the contentions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner and the grounds made in the application.

In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court stands vacated.

End.
